overview: It’s time for another deep dive! This time we’ll be covering the Archer.

Like the Wizard and Spellblade, we’ve been testing out their new kit internally, fixing issues, and getting things in a solid state before it hits Beta. But as always, expect iteration as time goes on.
With that out of the way, let’s review some of the previously mentioned characteristics and see how they've evolved:

sections.title: Notes
paras: This one didn’t entirely pan out with the way our combat system works, but the new Strafing Barrage line allows you to fire multiple shots while moving, and the kit continues to have a number of instant-cast options.

This generated a lot of questions. Obviously it affects the theme of abilities, such as Smoke Bomb Arrow and Immobilizing Trap, but we’ve also decided to focus this into a unique way of acquiring abilities rather than an inventory space obligation. More on this below.
As mentioned above, the Strafing Barrage ability fulfills this item. It’s available early on in the toolkit and has multiple upgrades as you level.

Disengagement, a pre-existing ability, remains unchanged, though we'll evaluate the threat reduction portion as the kit gets more public playtesting. There’s also some polish work to do on the movement and network side of this ability.

Archers get a version of Hide called Sniper’s Blind After hiding for a few seconds, the flat damage portion of their Quick Shot gets a substantial increase. This feels pretty good as an opener if you have time to hide during the pull.
Now, let’s go over the changes themselves.

entries.name: “Can fire at a reduced speed while moving”
“Has access to specialty arrowheads, including explosive tips, entangling nets, concealing smoke, and more (key abilities require specific arrowheads, so what you carry matters)”
“Utilizes tinkered traps including caltrops, nets, and bombs; their tools feel crafted and mechanical, rather than foraged like a Ranger”
“Can fire a quick volley while repositioning”
“Can leap backward when enemies close in”
“Can temporarily conceal themselves to empower their first shot upon reemerging”

sections.title: Traps
paras: Outside of Caltrops, Archer traps are now learned through Tinkering. You’ll find schematics (recipes) on your spell merchant. Once the trap has been made, you can right-click it to learn the corresponding ability.
Trap abilities require a trap in your inventory as a reagent, but it only has a 5% chance of being consumed, so you don’t need to carry around stacks of them.

Since this is the first bit of Tinkering to make it in-game, you should probably expect these recipes to get some iteration as the tradeskill develops. The schematics are Archer-only and don’t require significant investment into Tinkering.

This trap continues to be learned through an ability scroll. It sees its duration increased and now deals damage over time to enemies within the area. We’ll watch for feedback on this one to see if players would rather lose the damage component to make it more group-friendly as a snare.

This ability has changed significantly. It's no longer consumed by an enemy stepping on it, and no longer has an interaction with Illuminating Shot (which has been removed). Now you set it up and explode it with Flare, which has additional uses beyond just light.
This ability remains largely unchanged, but we've reduced its chance to be broken by damage so that it's more in line with other roots.

This is a new trap with a simple purpose: to notify you when something, or someone, has entered its area and triggered it. It doesn't cause damage or threat, so you might consider using this to keep track of repops, roamers, or other forms of danger.
Another new trap. This one detonates when stepped on, poisoning enemies in a tight area around it.

entries.name: Caltrops
entries.desc: Scatter caltrops around yourself, decreasing the Movement Speed of targets within the affected area and dealing Physical Damage to them every few seconds.

entries.name: Oil Trap
entries.desc: Place an oil trap at your feet, dealing Fire Damage to nearby targets when detonated with Flare.

entries.name: Immobilizing Trap
entries.desc: Place a trap at your feet, immobilizing the first target that triggers it.

entries.name: Alarm Trap
entries.desc: Place an alarm trap at your feet, notifying you of targets that enter the affected area.

entries.name: Poison Gas Trap
entries.desc: Place a poison gas trap at your feet, dealing Poison Damage every few seconds to nearby targets when triggered.

sections.title: Stances
paras: The former stance Deadeye has been changed to a cooldown. Archers now have two combat stances in its place.
This is your go-to stance when soloing, and it's the first you’ll get while leveling.
You’ll get this one a bit later and find it works better when stationary.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries.desc: Adopt the role of a skirmisher, slightly increasing your Movement Speed, reducing the cooldown of Strafing Barrage, and reducing the cast time of all abilities.

entries.name: Marksman
entries.desc: Adopt the role of a marksman, increasing the damage of your Piercing Shot and Splintering Shot, and granting your ranged attacks and abilities a chance to land Critical Hits.

sections.title: Stealth and Mobility
paras: This is one of the big focuses around the Archer update. You won’t get Rogue-level stealth, but instead a bit of utility to reinforce the theme of a repositioning “sniper." Disengagement remains a useful mobility and threat reduction option.
A short combination of Sprint and Stealth that allows you to bypass an enemy pack or two, or perhaps set up a surprise attack in PVP.
Channel multiple shots while on the move. You still have to face your target, but you can use this while moving backwards or, as the name implies, strafing to stay aimed at the target.

This isn't actually an ability, but a trait instead. It gives you a small advantage when you can find a perch to shoot from. Currently you start with it, but that may change in a future revision to our Traits system.

entries.name: Sniper's Blind
entries.desc: Conceal your position, rendering you virtually undetectable. Additionally, your Quick Shot deals increased damage while concealed by Sniper's Blind.

entries.name: Relocate
entries.desc: Retreat into the shadows and relocate to a more advantageous position, increasing your Movement Speed and briefly rendering you virtually undetectable.

entries.name: Strafing Barrage
entries.desc: Barrage your target with arrows, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage four times. This ability can be used while moving.

entries.name: High Ground
entries.desc: Your damage dealt with a bow is increased when above your target.

sections.title: Damage and Debuffs
paras: The core abilities are staying, though some have been renamed. Aimed Shot is now Piercing Shot, and Multishot is now Splintering Shot (and has had its damage improved). Quick Shot remains a core damage dealer, but can now be used in conjunction with Sniper's Blind. Pinning Shot is now Net Shot, has no minimum range, and the temporarily disabled condition that required the target to hit a wall is gone for good.

Smoke Bomb Arrow, Flare, and Net Shot now require specialty arrows. These are crafted with Fletching, can be placed in your quiver, and can be used without equipping them in your ammo slot. They aren’t overly punishing to create, but do require a little preparation.
New archers start with this now and pick up Quick Shot shortly into their progression. This is a lower damage, instant cast shot with no minimum range.

Another instant shot that shares a cooldown with Quick Shot and Point Blank. Though it deals less damage up front, it causes your target to bleed, which is stackable up to 3 times. With good timing, you can weave this in between Quick Shots (or more easily, Point Blank) to keep the bleed stacks up. Bleeds will have some inter-class mechanics in later updates.
This is a crafted arrowhead that blinds enemies near your target.

entries.name: Point Blank
entries.desc: Fire a point-blank shot at your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage.

entries.name: Barbed Arrow
entries.desc: Fire a barbed arrow at your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Bleed Damage every few seconds.

entries.name: Smoke Bomb Arrow
entries.desc: Fire a smoke bomb at your target, blinding them and nearby targets. This ability requires a bow and Smoke Bomb Arrow.

sections.title: Cooldowns
paras: This is now received a bit later on, but better matches its name by working as a tertiary haste. It also resets the other new shots in the trio.
This is now received later in your progression, and is dodge-based instead of parry.
This is now a late-game cooldown.

entries.name: Flurry of Arrows
entries.desc: Prepare yourself to unleash a flurry of arrows, instantly resetting the cooldown of your Barbed Arrow, Point Blank, and Quick Shot abilities, and increasing your Ranged Attack Speed.

entries.name: This ability is considered a tertiary haste.
This ability resets the cooldown of Barbed Arrow, Point Blank, and Quick Shot a second time when it ends.
Anticipate
entries.desc: Anticipate enemy aggression, granting you a 100% chance to dodge incoming melee attacks.

entries.name: Deadeye
entries.desc: Lock onto targets with deadly precision, temporarily increasing all Ranged Damage dealt.

sections.title: Removed Abilities
paras: Distracting Shot, Purging Arrow, Scatter Shot, and Illuminating Shot have been removed due to being off-theme or not complementing the new kit.

overview: A common question after the initial Bard direction post seemed to be, “What exactly is the Bard’s role?” So, let’s begin by clearing that up. Bard is a versatile support class who focuses on supplying buffs that stack with other classes' signature buffs, crowd control, and pulling. The design of the bard forces them to choose just a few of the support facets they can provide at any one time, via their memorized songs, the songs they are actively maintaining, and the instrument they have equipped (and therefore the played songs that get amplified).

This update focuses on easing the amount of work required just to maintain buffs, increasing the variety of songs they have access to, and giving them a means to add damage to a group without maintaining a charmed pet. While instrument swapping is not directly addressed, the new casting mechanic and wielding style will hopefully reduce how often you feel obligated to do so, and this may see further iteration in the future.

sections.title: Stat Changes
paras: Charisma is now used to determine bard mana, as well as damage bonuses on songs. It would apply to healing as well, but Bards currently lack any such spell. Hymn of Restoration is a Health Regeneration stat buff, not an actual heal.

sections.title: Skill and Wielding Changes
paras: Bards no longer have access to the Dual Wield skill. While visually and thematically we tend to think of bards as capable of wielding a pair of fast weapons, the mechanics of the class are better suited to wielding a single weapon with an instrument in their off hand. Bards now gain the Double Attack skill at the same levels and caps they previously had Dual Wield.
Bards have lost the Channeling skill. This did nothing for them anyway, as their songs can only be interrupted via a stun.

Bards have also lost the Meditation skill. The vast majority of their spell lineup requires zero or minimal mana, and few Bards have the time to sit and do nothing anyway. With the changes to their casting mechanic, there’s a bit more incentive (or at least time) to use their Shout abilities, and these will need to applied strategically to make the best use of their mana.

sections.title: Casting Mechanics
paras: Bard songs which buff themselves or the group will now remain active after casting them and auto refresh after casting a new song. This has always worked this way for the most recent song, but bards are now able to maintain multiple. Initially, bards will play in “Cut Time” and maintain a 3 song Measure. At level 30, bards unlock the “Common Time” trait, adding a song to their Measure allowing them to maintain 4.

When you play another beneficial song and are already at capacity, the oldest song will stop being maintained and fade off quickly after. Alternatively, you can stop one of the active songs by using that ability, and start a new one without pushing the oldest out.
Your actively maintained songs are shown on the Ability Bar, with the most recently cast song highlighted in white.

When you cast a targeted or detrimental song, you’ll push a song out of your queue, and only the most recent song will be refreshed automatically. You’ll need to twist (sequentially recast the songs) to maintain multiple detrimental songs, or a combination of buffs and detrimental songs.

When not needing to actively recast songs to maintain buffs, you should have a bit more time to use the new melee ability, or your Shouts, which can be used while the songs in your Measure stay active.

sections.title: Instruments
paras: Instruments have been greatly increased in strength, with basic store-bought versions now adding a 50% bonus to applicable songs. All existing instruments have had their bonus value reviewed and set on this new scale. Healing Hymn and Hymn of Inspiration have had their base values adjusted as a result of the new scale for instrument bonuses. The instrument types for some songs has changed in this rework.
We hope to see more spells impacted by instrument quality in future patches.

entries.name: Instrument bonuses currently apply to the following spell types:
entries.desc: Stat bonuses other than Haste (including Movement Speed and Health Regeneration)

sections.title: Melee Ability
paras: Bards gain a single melee ability, Whistling Blade. This attack does modest damage, but applies a Strength buff. At higher tiers, this buff adds Armor Class and Haste (Primary). While this has no casting time, it does apply a short global cooldown and isn’t best used when frantically twisting your songs.

sections.title: Shouts
paras: Shouts are mana-consuming instant cast abilities Bards can use while maintaining songs, or between songs they are twisting. You cannot use a Shout during the 3 second cast time of a song.

entries.name: Bards retain all their current shouts:
entries.desc: The Screaming Vocalization DD line

entries.name: The Mesmerizing Whisper line of short duration mezzes
They gain one additional shout:
entries.desc: Paralyzing Shriek - Release a paralyzing shriek, stunning foes around you for 3 seconds

sections.title: Songs
paras: Songs are the bread and butter of the Bard toolkit, and are either twisted or multiple songs can be maintained in a set of active songs called a Measure. In this rework, some songs may have changed their Instrument type. Each Instrument type has at least one song that scales numerically with the quality of the instrument.

entries.name: The Siren’s Call line of Bard Charm songs has received a few changes:
entries.desc: Only Beasts and Humanoids can now be charmed

entries.name: Charms no longer have a chance to break when damaged
The Damage of Charmed NPCs is now reduced to be on-par with the damage of a dedicated pet class’ pet.

sections.title: Mesmerization
paras: Somniferous Serenade is now a Wind instrument song, but is otherwise unchanged. Mesmerization songs now handle overwrites based on duration, making it easier to work with an Enchanter to replace short lasting Bard mezzes with longer lasting Enchanter versions.

sections.title: Damage over Time songs
paras: The Dissonant Riffs line has been removed. This line included 5 songs that stacked, but it wasn’t obvious to all players that they could be used together and stack, and were often misinterpreted as upgrades that had the numbers or descriptions set wrong.

The new Vellicosa’s Fanfare line features two Brass-based magic DoTs that specifically call out in their description that they stack together. The higher level one, Vellicosa’s Tantara, adds bonus damage when the target is already affected by Vellicosa’s Fanfare. The total damage of these two songs is an upgrade over the total of the previous 5 DoTs - this is strictly an upgrade.

sections.title: Haste Songs
paras: These songs have been renamed to be more easily understandable by players that are not real life musicians, but are otherwise unchanged. In addition to their Primary Haste songs, Bards continue to offer top-tier Secondary Haste, allowing them to further buff groups that already contain an Enchanter or Shaman.

sections.title: Resist Songs
paras: Resistance buffs are an area the now Bard excels at. The previous two Magic Resistance songs that mimicked resistance buffs other classes get have been replaced with 4 scaling buffs that can be further improved based on your equipped Percussion instrument:
Bard resistance songs stack with resistance buffs provided by other classes.

entries.name: Chant of Magic Protection - provides 5 to 10 Magic Resistance before the instrument bonus
Chant of Purity - provides 5 to 10 Poison and Disease Resistance before the instrument bonus
Chant of the Elements - provides 5 to 10 Fire, Cold, and Electric Resistance before the instrument bonus
Chant of Neutrality - provides 5 to 10 Holy and Corruption Resistance before the instrument bonus

sections.title: Other songs
paras: While versatility is a defining aspect of the Bard, the existing songbook was rather sparse, and this rework beefs that out with some new song types. Expect to see a few more show up in the future.

entries.name: Beats of Battle - Beats of War has been moved to a higher level and the low level version replaced with this more modestly named version. Beats of War is an upgrade to Beats of Battle.

Aristam’s Steady Tread - Not every situation allows for the full speed of Bard’s Song of Travel, and Steady Tread fills the gap when a Bard finds themselves deep in a dungeon. The song offers a modest base run speed increase and the option to push that a bit further with an equipped drum.
Disenchanting Blare - A targeted Brass song to remove harmful effects from your party members.
Discordant Purge - The complementary song to Disenchanting Blare, this song dispels beneficial effects on your targeted foe.
Tembror’s Booming Bravado - Amplifies the voices of your groupmates, giving them a chance to fully resist Silence effects

Aristam’s Aerial Aria - This airy tune slows the descent of your group. While not making them immune to gravity or falling damage, it will decrease the rate at which they fall. Expect a pass on these levitate effects in the future to make them a bit safer, and use with caution for now.
Aristam’s Voluminous Voyage - This high level Percussion song combines the effects of Song of Travel, Sonnet of the Unseen, and Aerial Aria for the ultimate in bard travel.
Faedawyn's Piping of Protection - Weave a mail of musical protection around your group, increasing their Armor Class and absorbing incoming damage.
Anthem of Restoration - This high level upgrade song combines the effects of Healing Hymn and Hymn of Inspiration.

sections.title: Retained Songs
paras: Bards retain the following songs that haven’t been previously mentioned:

entries.name: Bards gain one new long cooldown ability:
entries.desc: Crescendo - Raise your song in a mighty crescendo, increasing your Instrument bonus with all Instruments, as well as Singing.

sections.title: Closing
paras: That wraps it up for this Bard update. We’re looking forward to seeing all you future Bards when Early Access opens up!

overview: Beastmaster is getting a fairly large rework, shifting from a Shaman-based hybrid to a beast-taming berserker theme. The spellbook is going away, but mana as a resource is staying. Mana now represents the shared bond with your chosen beast and, for the most part, is only used for abilities that interact with them. New melee abilities and pet-focused utility are replacing the shared Shaman spells.
Let’s jump right into this deep dive with the reason most of you are playing a Beastmaster - the pets!

sections.title: Pets
paras: Beastmaster pets are still obtained through the use of Bestial Bond, leveled up through an experience system, and fed based on a specific diet. This update lowers the experience needed to level your pets, making it easier to maintain multiple and supporting the practice of swapping between them via the Kennel Master.

Sharks are currently still tameable, but this will be going away soon and made unlockable via a quest during Early Access. The ability to tame more mythical beasts is likewise planned as a future quest unlock.

sections.title: Pet Roles
paras: Beasts are now split into DPS, Tank, and Balanced roles, and have variations in their stats to support this. Expect some iteration on the exact stat variations as we go from this patch into the next. DPS pets deal increased damage, and Tank pets have increased AC and health. Balanced pets deal slightly more damage and have slightly increased health.

We know that pet damage and survivability are key issues for players, so we’re working hard to nail the tuning on those. We’ll share the goals we're working toward, even if the rework patch (0.26.0) doesn’t quite get the pets into their final state.

We want Beastmaster to be a competitive DPS class, with their damage coming from both their own abilities and their pet’s. Expect to deal comparable damage to other DPS classes when using a DPS pet, with your pet making up a little less than half of your total damage. When using a Tank pet and the Guardian Spirit buff, expect your pet to be able to tank for solo and small group encounters.

sections.title: Pet Abilities
paras: Your choice of pet should matter more than just a skin and a few stat points. In this rework, each pet family will be getting a unique, utility-focused ability. For example, Spider pets will be able to root opponents in place with a web. We’ll save the details of the rest so you can discover them once you get your hands on the update.

sections.title: Pet Buffs and Heals
paras: Many abilities that previously required your pet to be targeted, such as the Spirit buffs or the Patch Companion line, no longer have this requirement, making them easier to use.

sections.title: Swarm Pets
paras: As mentioned in the initial update post, Swarm pets as they existed are going away. For the most part, you’ll be adventuring with a single companion, but new Kinship abilities will let you call upon the services of other animals for more specific situations.
Kinship: Bat is a placeholder until a proper bird model exists in the game. This ability briefly summons a bat pet to blind your target, without impacting your primary pet.
Kinship: Rat is a planned future ability that summons a controllable stealthy rat for scouting. Sadly it didn't make it into the initial rework patch, but we hope to make it available soon.
As the world grows and new beasts are added, you may find more to recruit into your service in this manner.

sections.title: Companion-Focused Abilities
paras: The update sees several new and improved abilities to help the Beastmaster support their pet.

entries.name: Bestial Bond - Appeal to the senses of a target beast, bonding it to your side.
Revive Companion - Rally your pet, returning it to life.

Mend Companion (changed) - Mend your pet, restoring Health over 12 seconds. (This spell line is now a heal over time and significantly more powerful, though at the cost of more mana. You won’t be spamming heals on your pet anymore, freeing you up to deal more damage yourself.)
Shrink Companion - Shrink your pet, reducing their overall size.
Cleanse Companion (new)- Cleanse your pet, removing Disease and Poison effects.
Invigorate Companion (new) - Reinvigorate the bond with your pet, instantly resetting their abilities and your Command: Kill and Command: Protect abilities.

Savage Spirit - Awaken a savage spirit within your pet, increasing their Attack Speed, Agility, and granting them a chance to activate Rip on melee attacks. (This is your offensive “Spirit” buff. Pets can only have one Spirit buff at a time.)
Guardian Spirit (new)- Invoke your pet's guardian spirit, reducing their Physical Damage received and the cooldown of their Provoke ability. (This is your defensive “Spirit” buff.)
Command: Kill - Command your pet into action, calling on them to perform a devastating attack. (“Command” abilities share a cooldown.)
Command: Protect (formerly Resource Guarding) - Command your pet to protect you, reducing all damage received while transferring some of it to your pet.

sections.title: Auras
paras: Beastmasters retain their group buffing aura, albeit with a slight rename, and gain another useful group buff. Though they've lost Speed of the Wild, Prowler’s Instinct offers a unique alternative with the advantage of being usable indoors.

entries.name: Predatory Instinct (formerly Pack of the Predator) - Awaken a predatory instinct in your group, increasing their Offense and Agility.

Prowler’s Instinct (new) - Awaken the prowler's instinct in your group, increasing their Movement Speed and rendering them undetectable to targets while behind them. (This ability grants the benefits of Sneak while increasing your movement speed, enabling a cautious group to skirt around some encounters they’d rather not engage in.)
Buffs
entries.desc: Sight of the Beast (new) - Imbue your sight with bestial clarity, enhancing your vision in darkness. (This ability grants you an Infravision equivalent.) Sight of the Predator (new) - Imbue your sight with predatory clarity, greatly enhancing your vision in darkness while reducing it in bright light. (This ability grants you an Ultravision equivalent.) Hunter’s Chase (formerly Speed of the Predator) - Embody a predator in relentless pursuit, briefly increasing your Movement Speed. Aquatic Affinity (new) - Attune yourself to aquatic beasts, increasing your Swimming skill and greatly decreasing your air consumption.

sections.title: Melee Abilities
paras: Strike has been replaced with several new attacks, most of which have a bias toward slower, two-handed weapons. For the claw / dual wield enthusiasts, Maul is a solid option.

entries.name: Enraging Strike (new) - Strike your target in a furious rage, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage and increasing the Strength, Dexterity, and Agility of both you and your pet. This ability shares a cooldown with other Might abilities.

Savage Strike (new) - Savagely strike your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage. Additionally, this ability gains a damage bonus if the target is bleeding. This ability shares a cooldown with other Might abilities. (Bleed effects can be applied by your pet when buffed with Savage Spirit, or by Rogues and Archers.)

Chop (new) - Viciously chop your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage, and creating an opening that causes your pet to land Critical Hits. This ability requires a two-handed weapon, and shares a cooldown with other Martial abilities.
Maul (new) - Violently maul your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage per equipped weapon and decreasing their Physical Damage dealt. This ability shares a cooldown with other Martial abilities.
Mangle (new) - Mangle your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage and reducing incoming healing effects. This ability requires a two-handed weapon and shares a cooldown with other Martial abilities.
Other Abilities
entries.desc: Pounce (new) - Leap toward your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage and increasing the Movement Speed of your pet. (The movement speed component here helps your pet keep up with you.) Howl of Dominance (new) - Exert dominance over your target, decreasing their Physical Damage dealt and increasing yours by the same amount. Call of the Faithful (new) - Call out to your stowed pets from a great distance, summoning one to replace your current pet. (This is a late game utility that allows you to change your current pet without visiting a Kennel Master.) Bestial Glimpse (new) - Bind your vision to that of a target beast, granting you the ability to see through their eyes. Lick Wounds (new) - Pause to mend your wounds, restoring Health at the cost of Mana every second. This ability is channeled. (This self-heal is best used out of combat to quickly get you back in action after a difficult fight.) Beastmasters also share the Lull Beast and Preservation (mount resurrection) line of spells with the Druid.

overview: Clerics are the premier healer: a versatile, faith-powered support class built to keep their group alive, while still bringing holy damage and utility to the table. With this update, we've given Clerics an entirely unique toolkit (several of their core spells used to be shared with other classes), rounded them out with a few new spells, and added some polish to existing spells.

Overall, Clerics remain close to their current form as a strong group healer with useful utility (cures, dispels, resurrection), a damage kit that leans into holy and anti-undead themes, and a few unique and valuable buffs. We've expanded several existing spell lines with more ranks to make the pace of upgrades more consistent, added new spell lines to fill in gaps, and removed a few spells that felt redundant or underused.

Clerics have also picked up a new starting trait: “Blessed.” As a class so tightly bound to their faith, Clerics enjoy a favored status, and thus may occasionally receive divine help on their adventures.

sections.title: Defensive Upgrade
paras: We've changed the way our armor class system works to provide more defense to heavier armor types. This means that plate armor is more effective at reducing incoming damage than it was before.

We've also given Clerics the Block skill as part of their Prayer of the Faithful self-buff. This increases the defensive benefits you get from shields by reducing incoming damage when you block a hit.

sections.title: Heals
paras: Healing is what Clerics do best, and they now have Cleric-specific versions of their core heals rather than sharing generic spells with other classes.

entries.name: Heal
entries.desc: Heal your target, restoring Health. (This is your bread-and-butter single-target heal, with a moderate cast time and heal amount.)

entries.name: Circle of Healing
entries.desc: Heal your group, restoring Health. (This is a strong emergency group heal on a cooldown.)

entries.name: Healing Light
entries.desc: Shine a healing light on targets in a frontal cone, restoring Health. (This is a great way to top off a group when multiple people are hurt. It now has a cast time, so it's a deliberate choice rather than a free upgrade over your single-target heal.)

entries.name: Promise of Mending
entries.desc: Bestow a promise of mending on your target, restoring Health after a few seconds. (This is a delayed heal, handy for topping someone off ahead of an incoming hit. This spell line was renamed from Impart Blessing; the spell itself works the same way it always has.)

entries.name: Blessed Barrier
entries.desc: Shield your target with a blessed barrier, absorbing damage received. (This is best applied before damage lands, rather than after. The barrier only lasts a short while, and any unused absorption is lost once it expires. Its mana cost per point of damage mitigated is roughly equivalent to a standard heal, so you’ll want to weigh its instant cast time against the risk of wasted absorption.)

sections.title: Damage
paras: Clerics aren't a DPS class, but their holy magic gives them real teeth, especially against the undead.

entries.name: Rebuke
entries.desc: Strike your target with divine energy, dealing Holy Damage. (This is your standard nuke that works on all target types. Formerly the Shock line.)

entries.name: Smite the Dead
entries.desc: Smite a target undead with holy light, dealing Holy Damage. (This hits noticeably harder than Rebuke, both per-cast and over a sustained fight, but it only works against undead targets. It was renamed from Repel the Dead and its damage has been improved.)

entries.name: Holy Strike
entries.desc: Strike down your target with holy energy, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Holy Damage. (This is a melee-based attack learned at level 1, giving you something to do in combat besides casting. It also has a small chance to channel the wrath of your faith.)

entries.name: Holy Fortitude
entries.desc: Bestow holy fortitude upon your target, increasing their maximum Health. (This spell is largely unchanged, but it now automatically heals your target for the amount of health gained, so you don’t need to top them up after casting it.)

entries.name: Hymn of Fortitude
entries.desc: This is a group-wide version of Holy Fortitude. It requires a reagent to cast.

entries.name: Blessing of Devotion
entries.desc: Bestow your target a blessing of devotion, increasing their maximum Health. Additionally, if your target falls to low Health while the blessing is active, it restores Health and the blessing fades. (This buff also increases maximum Health and stacks with Holy Fortitude. It provides an emergency heal when things get dicey, but requires a reagent to cast.)

entries.name: Prayer of the Faithful
entries.desc: Call upon your faith, increasing your Strength, Mana Regeneration, Secondary Mana Regeneration, and Block, granting you a chance to activate Fulfillment on melee attacks and the ability to see magical effects when considering targets. (This is the Cleric's signature self-buff, rolling several older spells, including the old Supplication line, into one long-lasting package.)

entries.name: Divine Aegis
entries.desc: Surround yourself with a divine aegis, granting you immunity to all incoming damage for 15 seconds. (This is your emergency panic button.)

entries.name: Inhibit Pain
entries.desc: Inhibit pain in your target, reducing all damage received for a few seconds.

sections.title: Retained Spell Lines

Redemption (renamed from Resuscitation; your resurrection spells)

Oath of Protection - Clerics already carry plenty of cooldown-gated defensive tools between Divine Aegis, Inhibit Pain, and Blessed Barrier. Oath of Freedom - Though there was no direct replacement to this spell, Clerics instead gained Circle of Healing, which felt like a more useful cooldown overall. Snare the Dead - Clerics already carry a dedicated anti-undead nuke and fear, and can fall back on their normal root against undead targets. Cure Blindness - This spell is being removed across all classes as we revisit them. Blind effects are typically short and low-threat, so a dedicated cure spell wasn't pulling its weight.

overview: Druids are a well-rounded class that can provide healing, DPS, and support. They often feel okay in these roles, but never particularly great at any one of them. With the class update, we’re adding the concept of “Seasons” to Druids, allowing them to temporarily specialize in healing, damage, or a hybrid of both.

Overall, Druids have not shifted far from their current incarnation on the Beta server. They’re strong soloers, capable healers who can still deal damage, and have a broad set of utilities that make them both self-reliant and valuable to groups. We’ve added some depth and scaling to some of their existing spell lines, but tried to refine rather than change the class.
Now, let’s dive into the new Druid feature we’ve added: Seasons.

sections.title: Seasons
paras: Seasons are a simple idea: the Druid gets a buff based on the season they're currently in. Summer is great for life and healing, Winter is for wrath and damage, and Spring and Autumn are a bit more well-rounded.

All four seasons should be equally valuable depending on the situation or play style of the Druid. Summer and Winter are the specialist seasons, whereas Autumn and Spring are the balanced Druid's domain. Note that seasons are completely independent of the in-game calendar, and each Druid in a group can be in different seasons at the same time.

entries.name: Summer - Lush and full of life, Summer is the season of growth and prosperity. While in Summer, the Druid gets a 20% bonus to healing and regeneration effectiveness. They also get access to a unique healing spell line, starting with Summer’s Warmth at level 8.

Autumn - Moving out of Summer, Autumn is the bountiful season of the harvest. While in Autumn, the Druid gets a 10% bonus to healing and regeneration effectiveness, as well as extra mana regeneration.

Winter - Cold and dark, Winter is the season of survival. While in Winter, the Druid gets a 20% bonus to damage spells and DoTs. They also get access to a unique damage spell line, starting with Winter’s Chill at level 8.
Spring - Hints of life come to the lands, but in Spring, the chill of winter still lingers. While in Spring, the Druid gets a 10% bonus to damage spells and DoTs, as well as extra mana regeneration.

sections.title: Seasonal Exclusive Spells
paras: Summer and Winter have a unique, season-exclusive spell. If you’re the main healer for a group, you’ll want to spend most of your time in Summer. If you’re filling the role of a damage dealer, Winter is your best bet. Here’s what the seasonal spells do:
This is a mana-efficient, fast-casting heal. It typically heals for a smaller amount than something like Greater Heal, but when used alongside the Touch of Nature line, it gains a substantial boost.
This is a mana-efficient direct-damage spell that deals cold damage. When paired with the Embers DoT line, the damage is enhanced, making it a valuable tool in the offensive Druid’s arsenal.

entries.name: Summer’s Warmth
entries.desc: Bless your target with the warmth of summer, restoring Health. Additionally, if the target is under the effect of any spell in the Touch line, this spell gains a healing bonus.

entries.name: Winter’s Chill
entries.desc: Freeze your target with winter's chill, dealing Cold Damage and decreasing their Movement Speed. Additionally, if the target is under the effect of any spell in the Embers line, this spell gains a damage bonus.

sections.title: Mantle of Summer and Mantle of Winter
paras: These two new buffs are essential to the Season system. They allow the Druid to pick a starting season for their play session, or quickly jump to another season when needed. Mantles are on a shared 20 minute cooldown and last one hour.

entries.name: Mantle of Summer
entries.desc: Wrap yourself in a mantle of summer, reducing the Mana cost of your Alteration spells, increasing your Armor Class, and granting you a Damage Shield that deals damage when hit. Additionally, this spell sets your current season to Summer.

entries.name: Mantle of Winter
entries.desc: Wrap yourself in a mantle of winter, reducing the Mana cost of your Evocation spells, increasing your Armor Class, and granting you a Damage Shield that deals damage when hit. Additionally, this spell sets your current season to Winter.

sections.title: How Seasons Change
paras: The Druid's current season is driven entirely by what spells they cast. By casting spells associated with the current season (e.g. healing spells in Summer), they remain anchored there. If they cast spells of the opposite type, they’re pushed toward the next season.

Each season is represented by a buff, which can stack up to a maximum of 10 (having more stacks does not increase the intensity of the buff, however). As you cast spells associated with the current season, you add to these stacks. Casting spells of the opposite type removes these stacks. When the season’s buff counter hits zero, the season ends and you transition into the next one. You start each new season with six stacks of the seasonal buff.

A dedicated main healer can stay in Summer as long as they focus on healing, while a dedicated DPS can anchor in Winter the same way. A Druid who leans toward one role but wants to weave in some of the other should aim to anchor in Autumn or Spring. The system rewards short-term commitment to a role without locking anyone out of switching.

We’ve found it to be a pretty intuitive system once you play with it. Since the seasons shift based on what you’re casting, you tend to automatically gravitate toward a season that matches your current play style; and every 20 minutes, you can reset your Season by casting one of the Mantle spells.

sections.title: Druid Spell Lines
paras: Now that we’ve gone over seasons, let’s take a look at the updated spell lines for Druids.

sections.title: Damage
paras: Druids aren't typically a dedicated DPS class, but that doesn’t mean they don’t have the tools to be one. They have access to powerful direct damage spells, multiple DoT lines of varying elements, and an AoE option for outdoor encounters.
This replaces the Moonfire spell line.
This spell line no longer stacks up to three times, but it does provide extra damage when used with the Winter’s Chill line. We’ve also tweaked the damage values a bit.
Gust of Wind doubles as an interrupt, which gives it value beyond raw damage in fights.
While this is the only AoE in the Druid's kit, it’s a strong one at the higher ranks.

sections.title: Heals
paras: Druids are a healing class first. They have a strong range of spells for keeping their party alive, covering everything from fast spot heals to long-duration regeneration.
This is your standard heal. Nothing fancy, but it's reliable and available in all seasons.
The Touch line’s healing is split between an initial burst and a short heal-over-time. It’s good for targets who need help now, but aren't in any immediate risk of dying.
This is a long-duration regen that keeps ticking between pulls and during fights.

sections.title: Removed Spell Lines
paras: Druids had a lot going on. While working on this update, we wanted to focus on keeping them strong and familiar, but thin down some areas that felt unnecessary. Here are the main things that were removed with the update:
Thanks for taking the time to look this over, and for your participation in our ongoing Beta. We look forward to getting the Druid update launched very soon for you to try out!

entries.name: Whispers of Eth-es - We’ve added mana cost reductions to the new Mantle spells and faster mana regeneration with two of the seasons. We’ve also tuned spell costs for sustained play. With these changes, we felt that Whispers of Eth-es wasn’t really needed anymore.

Nature’s Respite - As an instant heal on a five-minute cooldown, this spell felt out of character for the Druid—like a leafy Lay on Hands. With the addition of the Summer’s Warmth line and the seasonal buffs, Druids will be more than effective healers without this in their toolbox.

AoE Lull, Irresistible Lull - We talked about this in a recent update, but generally speaking, lulls have been overly-powerful and diminish the danger we’d like to see in the game. Druids still keep a strong outdoor lull and a beast-specific lull, though.
Tree Form - We’ll be adding this back in the future as a quested spell. It’s a cool and thematic ability for Druids, but we’d like to do more with it than just sell it on a vendor.

Bear Pet - Somewhere along the way, we ended up with more pets than we ever intended. Ultimately, this didn’t feel like a key part of the Druid class, but we may still revisit it in the future as we know players love pets.
Beast Speech, Strength Buff, Summon Cureberries/Food/Drink, turning other players into animals - These didn’t make the cut as Druids already had a broad spell selection.
Brambly Tunic - This line of self-only damage shield buffs was merged into the Mantles, so the separate versions were removed.

Cure Blindness - We’ll be removing this from other classes as well. Blind spells are often short in duration and don’t pose a great threat. We’ll reconsider this in the future if we decide to add a dungeon full of blinding creatures. Say, that’s an interesting idea…

overview: Elementalists command the forces of fire, water, earth, and air, channeling that power both into direct magic and into a living elemental servant that fights at their side. This update leans harder into that partnership: your companion isn't just backup anymore, it's a real part of how your own spells work.

Two new signature spells put that partnership front and center. One is a strike your companion delivers on your command. The other is your new primary nuke, that hits harder and gains a bonus effect based on the elemental companion you have summoned. Beyond those two, your companion's summon matches your level rather than falling behind, and the buffs and heals that keep your companion fighting have grown alongside everything else.

As MnM's most pet-focused class, you'll want to rely on the Companion Strike as your main damage dealer. It is the biggest hit for the mana cost, and upgrades more often than your classic-style Blast nuke. The Blast is still helpful, both for damage and the extra elemental utility effects it causes, but we wanted to increase the connection between you and your elemental pet as your main damage source.
One thing we'd planned on in the original class overview, but decided against as we worked on the update:

entries.name: "Less: generic convenience conjurations" didn't happen. Food, Drink, Bandages, Manastones, and the elemental weapon-summon lines all carried through essentially unchanged. When talking with elementalist players, it was clear that they valued these spells and the utility they bring to a party and did not want to lose them. The one genuinely new elemental-themed conjuration is a Ring of Waterbreathing.
Companion Strike
entries.desc: Command your companion into a devastating attack. You spend the mana and your companion delivers the hit. The strike carries your companion's own element and does extra damage against elemental creatures. The damage on this strike increases based on your pet's intelligence, which enables it to channel your will more effectively.

entries.name: Elemental Blast
entries.desc: Blast your target with arcane energy, dealing Magic Damage. If you have an elemental companion summoned, this spell also deals damage in your companion's element, along with a bonus effect matched to that element. This is your primary nuke, and it always does a solid hit of Magic Damage on its own. Summon an elemental companion and the spell grows a second half in that element, along with a themed side effect - a burn, a chill, a snare, or a casting slow, depending on which companion you brought.

entries.name: Elemental Empowerment
entries.desc: Infuse your companion with elemental power, increasing their Attack Speed, sharing a portion of your own Intelligence, and restoring their Health over time. This spell gives your pet a hefty burst of stacking haste, an intelligence buff that scales with your own intelligence, and a solid amount of regeneration. However, this spell is also mana intensive so keeping it active on your pet is an investment. It's up to you to decide how to split your mana between Strikes, Blasts, and Empowerments - but they all have real value. This stacks with your normal long-duration 'Elemental Fury' line of pet buffs.

entries.name: Elemental Resurgence
entries.desc: Infuse yourself with elemental resurgence, letting your next companion-summoning spell resolve in a fraction of its normal time and for less mana. Handy after your companion falls in a hard fight, or any time you need to swap companions without eating the usual downtime.

entries.name: Speedy Companion
entries.desc: Infuse your companion with elemental speed, increasing their Movement Speed.

entries.name: Summoning Your Companion
entries.desc: Your four elemental servants - Water, Earth, Fire, and Air - summon and play the same way they always have. What's changed is the pace: your companion now stays in sync with your own level when summoned, up to the maximum for that summoning spell. You'll no longer get pet upgrade ranks for all four pets every four levels. Instead you'll unlock all pet types by level 12, and get a new rank every 16th level. However, each rank grows with you so your rank 1 Water Pet summon will give you a pet from level 1-15, based on your own level when summoning. There's no gap, as you'll get rank 2 when you hit level 16, which will summon Water Pets from level 16 - 31.

entries.name: Elemental Spellshield
entries.desc: Surround yourself with elemental power, increasing your Health, Armor Class, and Magic Resistance, plus your Cold and Fire Resistance, and granting you the ability to see magical effects when considering targets. Attackers who strike you are chilled and slowed. Your core self-buff, now merging the original Spellshield, Water Shield, and Sense Magic lines into a single self-buff.

entries.name: Ring of Water Breathing
entries.desc: Summon a temporary ring that grants Enduring Breath when worn - adding additional elemental-themed utility for you and your party.

entries.name: Fount of Mana
entries.desc: One benefit of your Water Pet is their Fount of Mana spell. This is a mana regen aura that benefits your party when you have a Water Pet summoned. We’ve updated this spell to now stack with Primary Mana Regeneration spells, so it’s additional mana regen that works with other buffs.

overview: Enchanters are one of our strongest and most unique classes, with high group utility and desirability. The Enchanter update was fairly light, focused on some quality of life changes where needed, but also a key adjustment to Charm to bring it more in line the intended power of the class.

Enchanters are primarily a group-focused class, which lines up with their unique and powerful kit of buffs, debuffs, and crowd control abilities. Mesmerize, charm, and stun give you more ways to take an enemy out of a fight than any other class, and a buff suite built on mana regeneration, haste, and mental stats makes you worth bringing along even when crowd control is not required.

Your mental buffs (Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma) consolidate into a combo buff, your core self-buff bundles a variety of effects into a strong package, your Shadowkin pet has less upgrade ranks but always summons at your own level, and two of your signature buffs now have a group-wide version for when you'd rather just cast it once. Charisma also pulls more weight than it used to, contributing to your damage spells, your runeskin, as well as Charm and Lull.

One key topic to talk about up front: Charmed NPC damage has been reduced from its previous level. While charmed NPCs are certainly weaker, they are still a strong source of extra damage in a group situation, and Enchanters are still able to solo by buffing their charmed pet, and debuffing their target NPCs. Certainly with weaker charmed pets, soloing will not be as efficient and fast as it was previously, but it is still viable.

This is a topic we've received lots of feedback on during Beta, and not everyone will agree with this change. In the past, charmed pet damage often exceeded the amount of damage you could get by adding 2-3 more DPS classes to a group, and was unquestionably the highest damage spell in the game by a wide margin. This change will be good for game balance, and allow us to tune difficulty to be more reasonable for diverse groups.
While we're highlighting this change in the Enchanter Deep Dive, this does affect the Charm spells of Elementalists, Druids, Bards, and Necromancers as well.

sections.title: Crowd Control
paras: Mesmerize, Charm, and your point-blank stun all work exactly as they always have - your CC suite was already the deepest in the game, and it didn't need reinventing. This is a unique and powerful kit that is the core strength of Enchanters.

One small tightening: your pacify line, which lulls enemies and makes it easier to split groups, now works on only one target at a time instead of several at once - similar to the changes we've made in previous class updates.

sections.title: Charisma and Power
paras: Charisma now has additional value for more of your kit. Your mental-affliction damage line, your channeled damage-over-time spell, and your rune shield all scale up further the more Charisma you have. Additionally, Charisma is still a key stat for Charm and Lull spells.
Three previously single-stat buffs - Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom - are now merged into a combined buff.

entries.name: Sagacity
entries.desc: Inspire your target, increasing their Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom.

sections.title: Vespyra's Veil
paras: Your core self-buff lasts an hour and combines many helpful effects you'd always want active. This replaces your spellshield line
It’s mentioned above, but enemies have a chance to be dazed briefly if they hit you, getting you a few precious seconds to get them under control or make your escape.

entries.name: Vespyra's Veil
entries.desc: Encircle yourself with a magical shield, increasing your maximum Health, Armor Class, and Magic Resistance. You also gain the ability to see invisible entities and sense magical effects, and attackers have a chance to be dazed when they hit you.

sections.title: Group Support
paras: Two of your signature buffs now have a group-wide version. Cast once, and your whole party gets the same benefit you'd otherwise be handing out one ally at a time. Both of these require a reagent, and are available to purchase on your spell vendor.

entries.name: Group Sagacity
entries.desc: Inspire your party, increasing their Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom.

entries.name: Group Enlightenment
entries.desc: Enlighten your party's minds, increasing their Mana Regeneration.

sections.title: Your Pet
paras: Your pet is still a solid source of damage, though it has been reduced some to differentiate it from the dedicated pet casters: Elementalist and Necromancer. Your Shadowkin now summons at your own level as you grow, instead of falling behind between upgrades.
