overview: Fighters are among the classes with the fewest abilities, so much of this update is additive and focused on filling out their toolkit with satisfying upgrade paths. We’re introducing retaliation abilities and the Vengeance mechanic to their kit, allowing Fighters to continue dealing damage while solo or tanking for a group. Most of their current abilities remain intact, but expect some balancing adjustments as we tune numbers between classes. To set your expectations, we’re aiming for Fighters to do more DPS than most tanks, but less than a DPS-centric class like Ranger or Monk.

As a “master of arms”-themed class, Fighters now have a number of abilities requiring a specific weapon type. You’ll want to choose a loadout based on your weapons, or alternatively, bring multiple weapons and swap based on the encounter.

There’s also been a shake-up in regards to cooldowns. All Shouts are now on a shared cooldown, while Taunt no longer shares a cooldown with Unnerving Shout. Shield Bash is now on a cooldown with Shield Block instead of Frenzy.

sections.title: Retaliation / Vengeance
paras: This is a new mechanic specific to Fighters, granted automatically while in any of their three stances. When taking damage, you’ll have a chance to generate a stack of the Vengeance buff, which you can spend on a few abilities:

entries.name: Frenzy - Eviscerate your target with a frenzy of attacks, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage up to five times and increasing your Attack Speed. (This ability consumes all your Vengeance, performing a weapon strike for each stack consumed. It has a higher baseline damage than before, so the hits should feel a bit more satisfying.)
Cleave - Cleave through targets in a frontal cone, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage. (This 2H-based ability consumes one stack of Vengeance to hit up to three targets.)

Second Wind - Catch a second wind, restoring Health every few seconds. (This ability consumes one stack of Vengeance in return for a short-term regen. Vengeance stacks fade relatively quickly, so using this after a fight is a good way to burn any leftover stacks. The amount healed scales with your Stamina stat.)

sections.title: Stances
paras: Fighters retain their Offensive and Defensive stances, while gaining a third:

entries.name: Tactician Stance - Shift into a tactician's stance, increasing your resistance to Root, Stun, and Incapacitate effects. (This stance is useful for pulling, specific encounters, and likely PvP.)
Some existing abilities have been slightly adjusted:
entries.desc: Rend - Now has a chance to reset Cleave and Feint in addition to Frenzy and Shield Bash. Shield Bash - Now interrupts spell casting.

entries.name: In addition to Rend, Kick, and Clobber, Fighters gain:
entries.desc: Cross Cut - Cut through your target with dual weapons, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage per equipped weapon. (This is a DW-based attack on the same cooldown as Rend. It deals more raw damage than Rend, while lacking the ability to reset your cooldowns.) Feint - Outmaneuver your target with a feint, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage, decreasing their Agility, and knocking them off balance. (Since this attack is on the same cooldown as Frenzy and Cleave, it's best used when you don’t have Vengeance available to fuel other attacks. Monks can also take advantage of this “off-balance” state to empower some of their abilities.)

entries.name: In addition to Disarm and Armor Break, Fighters now have:
entries.desc: Kneebreaker - Smash the knees of your target, decreasing their Movement Speed.

entries.name: Ranged
entries.desc: Challenging Arrow - Fire an arrow of challenge at your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage, and increasing your Threat against them. (This is a high-threat pulling option, dealing marginally more damage than the base Shoot ability.)

entries.name: Other Abilities
entries.desc: Shield Block - Raise your shield in defense, temporarily absorbing damage received. (As implied, this ability requires a shield.) Juggernaut - Charge at your target like a juggernaut, immobilizing them. Additionally, your Threat generation is temporarily increased and all damage received is reduced. (This is a high-level alternative to Charge.) Vanguard - Impede enemy aggression toward your target, decreasing their Threat generation. (This helps you prevent a group member from pulling aggro off of you.)

overview: Inquisitors are a specialized tank class with a myriad of tools for neutralizing casters. They’ve always served this role well, so in this rework, we’ve focused on smoothing out the rough edges for that experience.

The fundamental role, theme, and broad strokes of the Inquisitor kit are staying the same. Overall damage is slightly increasing, particularly against casters. Several of the shared spell lines with Enchanters have been tweaked to be unique to the Inquisitor, and a few new tools have been added.

entries.name: Melee Abilities
entries.desc: Censuring Strike - Censure your target with a violent strike, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage, and decreasing their Casting Speed. (This ability combines Slam and the Mind Exhaustion spell line. Given its lack of mana cost, the Casting Speed reduction has been slightly rebalanced.) Purifying Blow - Unleash a purifying blow upon your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Magic Damage, increasing your Threat against them, and granting you a chance to remove one beneficial effect from them. Additionally, if the target is afflicted by any spell in the Distress line, the purge effect is guaranteed. (This ability has a longer cooldown, but deals more damage than Censuring Strike. It’s now tiered with slightly higher damage scaling, and the purge effect can occur even without the debuff.)

entries.name: Spell Lines
entries.desc: Distress - Distress your target, dealing Magic Damage, increasing your Threat against them, and decreasing their Magic Resistance. (This line combines a couple of spells, formerly shared with Enchanters, into a single one. When applied to your target, it guarantees the purge effect of Purifying Blow.) Pillage Mana - Pillage the mind of your target, draining Mana and distributing a percentage of the amount drained to each group member. Additionally, when this spell successfully lands on the target, its Mana cost is refunded. (This line replaces the Incinerate Mana line. It now has a 60-second cooldown.)

sections.title: Auras
paras: We’re making a few trades between previous spell lines and Inquisitor auras. Aura of the Inquisitive is being removed in favor of a new perk on the Pillage Mana line (see above), while the Haste spell line is being removed in favor of Aura of Rapidity. Weapon Shield has been removed, but Aura of Resistance remains.

entries.name: Aura of Rapidity - Envelop your group in an aura of rapidity, increasing their Attack Speed. (This effect is considered a Primary Haste, but includes a smaller Secondary Haste component that stacks with hastes from Enchanters and Shamans.)
Aura of Resistance - Envelop your group in a warding aura, reducing their Spell Damage received and increasing their Cold, Fire, Corruption, Holy, and Magic Resistance.

sections.title: Defense and Cooldowns
paras: Inquisitor cooldowns are mostly unchanged, but a few have been pruned. They continue to have access to Arcane Aegis, Arcane Protection, Dominate the Mind, and Magic Disruption Shell, while Deflect and Focused Concentration have been removed.
Though Inquisitors typically prefer dealing with spell-casting opponents, we’ve added a defensive option to help them survive against difficult melee opponents, albeit at a mana cost.

entries.name: Ward of Suspicion - Encase yourself in a ward of suspicion, absorbing damage received. Additionally, when an attacker breaks the ward, their Attack Speed is decreased.

sections.title: Crowd Control and Interrupts
paras: Inquisitors are retaining their existing options for Stun and Silence effects. The Mesmerize line has been slightly branched from the Enchanter’s version, and Kick has been replaced with a Shield-based interrupt.

entries.name: Interdiction - Condemn your target, increasing your Threat against them and incapacitating them. (This spell adds threat to the mesmerized target, rather than “mem-blurring” them.)

Reflecting Bash - Fiercely bash your target with a shield, interrupting their casting, dealing Magic Damage equal to the Mana cost of the interrupted spell, and preventing them from casting spells from the same school of magic.

sections.title: Buffs
paras: Quite a few buffs have been bundled into other abilities. The Haste line has been converted to an aura (see above), while the Strength and targetable Magic Resistance buffs have been merged into Arcane Tyrant.
The Holy Resistance buffs were off-theme, so they’ve been replaced with self-only buffs for Electric and Fire.
Inquisitors continue to have access to the Spellshield line, increasing Health, Armor Class, and Magic Resistance.

entries.name: Arcane Tyrant - Embody tyranny over the arcane, increasing your Strength and Magic Resistance, and granting you the ability to see invisible entities and magical effects when considering targets.

sections.title: Other
paras: Psychic Choke has received a small damage increase to account for the lost melee damage while it's being channeled.
Mana Burn, Invisibility, Purge, Dispel Magic, and Memory Fog remain unchanged.

overview: As mentioned in the initial class update post, one of the biggest change to Monks is thematic. They're pivoting away from the elemental theme toward a more traditional spiritual one. Most of the original Monk kit remains intact with the exception of Way of the Water, which has been removed with its associated group heal.

entries.name: The four “Way of”-stances have been remapped to three styles:
entries.desc: Sun Style - Assume a sun-based fighting style, increasing your Offense. Additionally, Celestial Strike reverberates through to your target's soul, dealing Magic Damage after a few seconds. Moon Style - Assume a moon-based fighting style, increasing your Dodge and Block. Additionally, Celestial Fury further increases your Block and reduces your Physical Damage received for its duration. Wind Style - Assume a wind-based fighting style, increasing your Movement Speed. Additionally, Celestial Fury grants you a chance to strike your target a second time on melee attacks.

sections.title: Feign Death and Pulling
paras: In this patch, we fixed a long-standing bug that prevented any chance of re-aggroing mobs after standing up from a feign. Though re-aggro after a feign is now possible, the chances of it occurring have been massively reduced to allow Monks time to adapt. Considering how long this bug has been present, it'll probably take a bit of tuning to dial this chance in.

We’ve also introduced a new change to how NPCs loiter after a successful feign. NPCs that have been damaged will loiter much longer than untouched ones, giving you a little more control over the timing when they reset. Maximum loiter times have been reduced overall as well.
Furthermore, Monks are gaining a couple abilities that should assist them with pulling and splitting packs of mobs:

entries.name: Pinning Throw - Throw a weapon at your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage and immobilizing them. (This is an upgraded version of Throw that briefly pins the target in place, allowing you to stagger one of the pack a bit behind the rest.)
Double-Handed Strike - Strike your target with both hands, knocking them back and decreasing their Movement Speed.
Monks gain a couple mobility tools beyond their Wind Style buff:
entries.desc: Flying Kick - Leap toward your target to deliver a devastating flying kick, dealing Physical Damage. This ability scales with your Dexterity. (This is your gap closer.) Fleet of Foot - Hasten your steps, increasing your Movement Speed. (This is a short-duration speed boost.)

entries.name: Melee Attacks
entries.desc: Round Kick - Deliver a crushing round kick to your target, dealing Physical Damage and granting you a chance to reset the cooldown of your Celestial Strike and Hundred Fist abilities. This ability scales with your Dexterity. Celestial Strike - Squarely strike your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Physical Damage, granting Celestial Fury, and granting you a chance to activate Celestial Vitality. This ability can be enhanced by your active Style. (This ability is mostly unchanged, but now also procs Celestial Vitality if your opponent’s Chakra is fractured. See Quivering Palm.) Hundred Fists - Pummel your target in rapid succession, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage four times. Additionally, if your target is off balance, you have a chance to stun them. (This attack shares a cooldown with Celestial Strike and can be reset by the Round Kick ability. The stun component can be triggered by Quivering Palm or a Fighter’s Feint ability.) Quivering Palm - Strike through your target and into their soul, inflicting increasingly debilitating effects with each strike. One strike knocks them off balance. Two strikes block their Chi, reducing their Physical Damage dealt. Three strikes fracture their Chakra, increasing their Physical Damage received. (This ancient and mysterious technique layers debuffs on your opponent, several of which amplify your other abilities.) Disarming Strike - Strike the wrist of your target, temporarily removing their weapon and reducing their Physical Damage dealt. Sweeping Kick - Trip nearby targets with a sweeping kick, stunning them. (This ability now also knocks your opponents off balance.)

sections.title: Body Mastery
paras: Monk training hones both the body and spirit, giving them a number of disciplines they can choose from. However, you can only have one body alteration ability active at a time:

entries.name: Spirit Sustenance - Suppress the need for sustenance, decreasing your food and drink consumption.
Slow Breathing - Slow your breathing, decreasing your air consumption while underwater.
Falling Petal - Move with the grace of a falling petal, reducing the effect of gravity on your body. (This ability compounds with your Safe Fall skill.)

Ascendant Body - Ascend your body to a state of perfection, simultaneously decreasing your food, drink, and air consumption, and reducing the effect of gravity on your body. (At the highest levels of mastery, Monks can command all of the body disciplines at once.)

sections.title: Defense and Cooldowns
paras: Monks keep their existing Mend and Stone Stance cooldowns, while gaining:

entries.name: Perfect Focus - Perfect your strikes through deep focus, causing melee attacks to temporarily land as Critical Hits.

Cyclone Staff - Spin your staff rapidly to deflect incoming blows, greatly increasing your Block chance and dealing Weapon Ratio Damage with each successful block. (This is a channeled ability that requires a two-handed staff.)
Iron Fists - Forge your fists into iron, temporarily nullifying the effects of Damage Shields.
Ethereal Body - Become nigh ethereal, increasing your Agility and Dodge chance.

overview: The Necromancer's fantasy is the Master of Death: a pet-focused caster who works from range while an undead minion holds the front line. It wears enemies down with corruption and decay, and takes life, strength, and power from everything you kill.
This update delivers more of that fantasy by trimming generic caster utility and deepening the things the class already owns.

Your damage-over-time spells are sharper, and they now hit undead targets for bonus damage up-front. Your minion scales with your level between spell ranks, so you'll always summon a pet of your own level. A new family of Pacts lets you pay with your own health for a stronger pet, faster afflictions, and your shield can now bind your minion to you when you're in trouble. Around the edges, several utility spells moved to new levels, a handful of redundant ranks were consolidated, and a few narrow spells were retired.

Two things we promised in the original Necromancer preview are not in this update: collectable pet types found through world exploration, and the ability to temporarily raise fallen enemies as additional pets. Both are still on our list, but we couldn't get to them before Early Access launch - and collectible pets in particular will roll out over time as we continue to add new zones and content to the game. Burning Bones is available as a quest reward, and is a great example of future collectible pets. The pets you have today (the skeleton, zombie, and ghoul lines) are the foundation we intend to build that collection on going forward.

sections.title: Death's Toll: Damage Over Time
paras: Corruption and decay are still your primary damage, and the three big damage-over-time lines are still the core of what you cast.

Bonus damage against undead. Deluge, Shadows, and Rot now deal bonus damage when they land on an undead target. The spell ticks as normal, and also hits immediately for a little extra. This replaces the old undead-only blast spells (Repel the Dead through Assail the Dead), which are gone. You no longer need a separate spell for undead. Your ordinary damage-over-time does the job now.
Pact of Eldritch Quickening makes all of these tick faster. See the Pacts section below.

entries.name: Deluge - a burst of poison damage followed by a lingering poison.
Shadows - Corruption damage over time that also snares your target. Each rank hits harder and lasts longer.
Rot - your disease line, now Rot Flesh, Rot Bones, and Rot Soul. Pure damage over time with no burst, and the most mana-efficient of your damage spells over a full duration.

sections.title: Life Drain and Transfer
paras: Everything the Necromancer takes from a victim goes somewhere: back into yourself, your pet, or into an ally.

entries.name: Life Drain - instant Corruption damage that heals you for the same amount. The line was cleaned up into a smoother climb across ranks.
Leech Lifeforce - the ticking version. It drains over time and heals you for what it takes.
Dark Embrace, Sacrificial Embrace, Corporeal Embrace - pay your own health to heal an ally in one burst.
Covenant of Life, Darkness, and Shadow - pay your own health to heal an ally over time.
Steal Strength (Lesser, regular, Greater, Superior) - take Strength from an enemy and add it to your own for a while. Transfer Strength does the reverse, giving your own Strength to an ally.

Mind Surge, Mana Surge, Mental Surge - gift mana to an ally. They now restore more, and cost more of your own mana to cast. These have a cooldown now, so they can come in handy in an emergency, but transferring your own valuable mana is not a constant activity.
Summon Lifestones - unchanged. A consumable heal you can conjure for yourself or a friend.

sections.title: The Pacts and the Red Line of Danger
paras: The Necromancer lives on the red line, trading vitality for power and knowing exactly how far to push it. The Pact family is the clearest expression of that. Every Pact costs you a slice of your own health and gives you something in return.
Two of the Pacts are old friends. Four are new.
A pet tank that keeps up with hard fights, paid for out of your own health.
A minion that feeds your group.
A smaller trade for a smaller gift. Useful in dark places.
The most direct "spend your body for damage" spell in the class. Instead of ticking every 6th second, your DoTs now tick every 5th second - getting their damage out a bit faster.

entries.name: Pact of Deathly Enduring
entries.desc: Bind your vitality to your pet, reducing your maximum Health and making them tougher: more Armor Class, more Health Regeneration and more maximum Health.

entries.name: Pact of Vampirism
entries.desc: Bind your life force to your pet, reducing your maximum Health and giving your pet a chance to drain life with its melee attacks, healing your group with what it takes.

entries.name: Pact of Coldlight
entries.desc: Bind your warmth to your pet, reducing your maximum Health and causing it to shed a cold, pale light over its surroundings.

entries.name: Pact of Eldritch Quickening
entries.desc: Quicken your afflictions, reducing your maximum Health. While active, your poison, corruption, disease and life-draining damage-over-time spells deal their damage faster.

sections.title: Blood Pact, Death Pact, and the Lich chain
paras: Your mana regeneration line follows the same curve it always has: Blood Pact, Death Pact, Shed Bones, Shed Flesh, Lich, and Arch Lich. Each trades your health every few seconds for faster mana regeneration, and each step up takes more health and gives more mana. The line lost one intermediate step (Demi Lich) and some ranks moved to new levels, but the trade is the same as it always was. Lich Spirit, the short high-cost burst at the top, is unchanged.

sections.title: Unliving Shield
paras: Your defensive buff, formerly Spellshield, lasts an hour and now bundles a few things you'd always want active. It raises your maximum Health, Armor Class, Magic Resistance, and now Holy Resistance, and it lets you sense magical effects while it lasts.

It also carries a new safety net, Soul Tether. If your Health falls low, your shield binds your minion to you for a short time, and your pet takes a share of the damage you would have taken. It can't trigger again for a while afterward, so treat it as an emergency measure rather than part of a defensive rotation. Your pet pays the price for your survival.

sections.title: Emergency exits
paras: Unholy Bulwark (a short window of immunity to all damage, usable even while stunned or feared) and Feign Death are unchanged. When the red line gets too red, these are how you step back.

sections.title: Your Minion
paras: Your minion is still the heart of the class, holding the front line while you work from range. The three main pet lines (Skeleton, Zombie, and Ghoul) are now short ladders of ranks instead of long lists of individual spells, and between upgrades your pet scales with your level, so it no longer falls behind while you wait for the next rank.

The three lines are different flavors of the same job, and each fights with its own abilities: skeletons use Strike, ghouls use Ghoul Tendrils, zombies use Zombie Drain, and all three use Provoke. These unlock at various levels, so you'll get your skeleton pet earlier than the rest.
The Pacts above are the other half of the bond with your pet, and the biggest change to how it plays.

entries.name: Summon Skeleton, Summon Zombie, Summon Ghoul
entries.desc: Reanimate the dead to fight alongside you. Each requires a reagent: bone chips for skeletons, zombie skin for zombies and ghoul skin for ghouls.

entries.name: Spectre Minion
entries.desc: Reanimate death incarnate. Your spectre is immune to Fear effects, and fights with Spectre Drain and Provoke.

entries.name: Burning Bones
entries.desc: Reanimate bone, conjuring a burning skeleton to serve you. Rank 1 of this pet is available as a quest reward for adventurous necromancers.

entries.name: Mend the Dead
entries.desc: Restore your pet's health. The line now has five ranks instead of three, so your pet heals keep pace with your pet across more of the game.

entries.name: Fury of Death
entries.desc: Stoke the fury of death within your pet, increasing their Attack Speed and Strength. Formerly Unrelenting Dead, and the first rank now arrives a little earlier.

entries.name: Summon Companion, Reclaim Essence
entries.desc: Unchanged. Summon Companion pulls your pet to your side, and Reclaim Essence destroys it and converts some of its health into mana.

entries.name: Dominion Over the Dead
entries.desc: Command the Dead and Dominate the Dead - take control of an undead target for a limited time and have it fight for you. Renamed from Charm, Beguile, Coax and Persuade the Dead. Restrain the Dead - incapacitate a single undead target. Now four ranks instead of one, so it stays useful as you level. Terrify the Dead - make an undead target flee. Formerly Fear the Dead. Lull the Dead - shrink an undead target's aggro radius. This can only affect one target at a time. Invisibility versus Undead - unchanged.

entries.name: Control and Escape
entries.desc: Fear and Deathly Howl - make one target, or everything near you, flee. Unchanged in function, and moved to new levels. Grasp of the Dead - hold a target in place. Ranamed from Root - Unchanged in function. Swirling Shadows and its ranks - your snare rides on this damage line (see Death's Toll). Feign Death - play dead and drop the threat of aggressive targets.

sections.title: Retained Spell Lines
paras: Several of these moved to new unlock levels as part of a full level-schedule pass.
Thanks for taking the time to look this over, and for your participation in our Beta. We look forward to getting your feedback after you try out the Necromancer update during Early Access!

entries.name: Damage
entries.desc: Deluge (poison burst with a lingering tick)

entries.name: Shadows (Corruption over time with a snare)
Rot (disease over time) - renamed from Malady, Infectious Disease, Shuddering Sickness, Afflicting Ailment, Irking Illness and Virulent Virus
Life Drain (instant Corruption damage that heals you) - higher ranks renamed from Life Sap, Life Siphon, Life Tap, Life Guzzle, Life Duct and Life Flume (now Life Drain II through VII)
Leech Lifeforce (Corruption over time that heals you) - higher ranks renamed from Leech Essence, Leech Spirit, Leech Soul and Leech Anima (now Leech Lifeforce II through V)
Pet
entries.desc: Summon Skeleton

entries.name: Fury of Death - renamed from Unrelenting Dead spell line
Buffs
entries.desc: Unliving Shield - renamed from Spellshield

entries.name: Blood Pact and the Lich chain
Cold Protection, Cold Resistance, Holy Protection and Holy Resistance
Healing and Transfer
entries.desc: Dark Embrace line

entries.name: Steal Strength line and Transfer Strength
Debuffs and Control
entries.desc: Spirit Splinter line (resist debuff)

entries.name: Fear, Deathly Howl, Grasp of the Dead (was Root), Lull the Dead
Command the Dead and Dominate the Dead - renamed from Charm the Dead spell line
Terrify the Dead - renamed from Fear the Dead
Utility
entries.desc: Gate

entries.name: Eye of the Underworld (formerly See Invisibility, now also senses magical effects)
Removed Spell Lines
entries.desc: Repel the Dead, Beset the Dead, Rebuff the Dead, Beleaguer the Dead, Assail the Dead - your undead-only blast spells. Their job now belongs to your damage-over-time spells, which hit undead harder. Sense Magic - folded into Unliving Shield and Eye of the Underworld rather than taking a slot of its own. A handful of intermediate ranks on the Life Drain, Mind Surge, resist debuff and mana regeneration lines that only existed to fill a level slot.

overview: With Paladin, we originally sought to create more distance from Cleric - leaning more into its melee and close quarters abilities. Paladin was already a complete class, but needed more flavor and excitement to complete its theme and make it more appealing to players. However, as the Cleric rework progressed and the miracles and blessings attached to their Holy Strike were well received, we walked back on this a bit. We’re still making more of their current kit distinct from their healer brethren, but brought the miraculous smites Cleric players have been enjoying over to their tank counterparts.
Paladins are losing Deflect, Weapon Shield, and Focused Concentration, as well as seeing Kick replaced with Shield Slam. These are changes going in for all the Knights.
Additionally, the Paladin Pet ability Ancient Guardian, has been removed due to being odd, off-theme, and generally too powerful.

Consecrations are a major new mechanic for Paladins to interact with, and offer a combination of offensive and defensive benefits. The Auras granted by Paladin have shifted around somewhat. Two new Oath abilities offer a way for the Paladin to defend a groupmate through sacrifice.
There’s some fun stuff to investigate, so let’s dig in.

sections.title: Supplication and Fulfillment
paras: Supplication has been removed from the Paladin ability list. The Strength and Mana Regeneration it provided have been moved into the Conviction buff, and the Fulfillment stacks are no longer consumed by Restorative Smite. The haste from fully stacking fulfillment has been pulled into the Fervor buff you may rarely receive from Crusader Strike.

entries.name: Crusader Strike
entries.desc: This is the Paladin’s basic attack, replacing Slam. Mechanically very similar to Holy Strike from the cleric line, but with a higher base damage and multiple tiers for more fine tuning across level ranges. This attack deals Weapon Ratio damage plus Holy Damage, with scaling bonus Threat. Like Holy Strike, it has a small chance to channel the wrath of your faith or filling you with Fervor, a small haste buff.

entries.name: Restorative Smite
entries.desc: Restorative Smite is a longer cooldown attack that shares a cooldown with its more damage-focused sibling, Vengeful Smite. Restorative Smite no longer requires a stack of Fulfillment to trigger its healing and can be used for consistent, if small, group healing. The damage has been reduced, but the ability maintains its bonus Threat. The healing is significantly amplified when standing upon consecrated ground - blessed by one of your two beneficial Consecration abilities.

entries.name: Vengeful Smite
entries.desc: This is the damage focused alternative to Restorative Smite. It deals Weapon Ratio Physical Damage plus Holy Damage, along with bonus Threat. Like Restorative Smite, when standing upon consecrated ground the Holy Damage you generate will be greatly increased.

entries.name: Hammer of Light
entries.desc: This is a new DD ability that can be used on targets dead and living, dealing Holy Damage and a bit of Threat. It is primarily a tool for pulling.

entries.name: Shield Slam
entries.desc: Shield Slam is a spell interrupt and school lockout that replaces the Kick ability in the old list.

entries.name: Warding Slam
entries.desc: An upgrade to Shield Slam, this ability gains damage based on the AC of the shield, and increases your Block % for a short duration after the ability is used. You do not need to interrupt a spell in order to benefit from the damage and block increase.

entries.name: Shield Toss
entries.desc: Shield Toss has been slightly changed from an AE to an actual bounce effect that chains between nearby targets, interrupting each target hit. This ability was always useful but fell a little flat on fun factor without any visuals, but now has VFX that shows the bouncing shield.

sections.title: Auras
paras: Paladins have two auras to choose from, each offering unique bonuses for their group.

entries.name: Aura of Courage
entries.desc: A defensive aura granting you and your group Armor Class as well as a small chance to fully resist Fear effects. While in this Aura, you’ll also receive a bonus to all your generated Threat.

entries.name: Aura of Piety
entries.desc: This aura grants a bonus to all healing received by members of your group.

sections.title: Consecrations
paras: Consecrations are ground based abilities that bless the ground upon which the Paladin stands - offering protections to those that stand within, or purifying the area from enemies. Consecrations remain where they were invoked for 30 seconds.

entries.name: Hallowed Ground
entries.desc: This simple blessing offers Corruption resistance to groupmates that stand within, while increasing the effectiveness of your Smite abilities.

entries.name: Blessing of Sanctuary
entries.desc: Formerly a targeted ability with a blocking buff to prevent reuse, Sanctuary will now protect those who stand within, reducing melee damage received.

entries.name: Exorcism
entries.desc: Sanctifies the ground under your feet, causing Undead within it to be snared and feared, and damaging any that defy you or return over time for the duration.

sections.title: Oaths
paras: A Paladin has vowed to protect their allies, which they express through two Oath abilities.

entries.name: Oath of Vigilance
entries.desc: A minor oath that absorbs 5% of the damage intended for a groupmate and redirects half of that damage to you. This is a long duration buff you can keep on an target.

entries.name: Oath of Sacrifice
entries.desc: A major oath that absorbs 75% of the damage intended for a groupmate and redirects half of that damage to you. This is a short duration buff on a longer cooldown.

entries.name: Conviction
entries.desc: Conviction replaces the short term Supplication buff, granting you Strength, Wisdom, and Stamina as well as minor Mana Regeneration.

entries.name: Poison and Disease
entries.desc: Paladins have two tiers of self-only resistance buffs against Poison and Disease

entries.name: Divine Spark
entries.desc: Paladins retain the Divine Spark hit point buff, which stacks with the Cleric line. They have lost access to Holy Fortitude and the other cleric hp buffs.

entries.name: Healing Touch
entries.desc: This spell replaces the existing healing line for Paladins. It is a short range, fast casting heal with a moderate cooldown time. It’s not the most efficient healing spell around, and due to the cooldown time, you’ll likely want to use Restorative Smite with it when playing as a temporary or secondary healer.

entries.name: Resurrection
entries.desc: Paladins now receive a full line of Resurrection spells one tier behind Clerics, starting at level 16 and ending with Revival, the 75% experience resurrection at level 56.

entries.name: Retained Spell Lines
entries.desc: Lull - these have been updated to use the current Cleric lineup of Pacify spells, which affect a single target at a time.

entries.name: Ward the Dead - the full line of damage versus Undead.
Removed Spell Lines
entries.desc: Weapon Shield

overview: The Ranger's fantasy is the Wilderness Veteran: blades up close, a bow at range, and a lifetime of fieldcraft that mixes a deep knowledge of the wild with some light woodland magic. Before this update, the class had drifted into something closer to a half-Druid, casting fire and borrowed nature spells between swings. This update pulls it back: the fire nukes, the fire and insect damage-over-time spells, and the elemental weapon and arrow enchantments are gone.

In their place is a fast martial kit built around your two weapons, four stances that change how that kit behaves, practical wound care, and a campfire ability that speeds your group's recovery between fights a few times an hour. What you were already good at stays: moving a group across open country, slipping past danger outdoors, calming beasts, and tracking your quarry.
You also live off the land, now foraging food, drink, and cureberries from the wild.

sections.title: Swordplay and Marksmanship
paras: Your combat abilities come in two sets, swordplay and marksmanship, and each set has an opener: Opening Strike for melee and Leading Shot for the bow. The two openers share a cooldown, so each time they're ready you pick one, melee or ranged.
Using an opener unlocks the follow-up abilities, then you can use one of them.
So the rhythm is: opener, one follow-up, opener again. And the choice each time is which follow-up the fight calls for.
Leading Shot and the marksmanship abilities need a bow, arrows, and a little distance between you and your target.
Your bleeds are your own, so two Rangers can bleed the same target without getting in each other's way.
For the pack that's closing in, or the group that's trying to run.
Formerly Truestrike. Only the name changed.

entries.name: Swordplay Abilities
entries.desc: Finishing Blow - Strike with both blades at once. Needs a weapon in each hand.

entries.name: Hamstring Slice - Cut at the target's legs and slow its movement.
Rending Cut - A cut that keeps bleeding after you hit. Landing it again before it wears off deepens the wound.
Marksmanship Abilities
entries.desc: Swift Shot - A hard-hitting, well-placed shot. Maiming Shot - A crippling shot that lowers the target's Dexterity, making its attacks less accurate. Barbed Shot - An arrow that leaves a bleeding wound. Repeat hits deepen it, the same way they do with Rending Cut.

entries.name: Tanglefoot
entries.desc: Snare several enemies in front of you at once. It only catches enemies, never your group.

entries.name: Apex Predator
entries.desc: A short burst of accuracy and damage you save for the right moment.

sections.title: Stances
paras: The old Imbue Weapon and Imbue Arrows spells wrapped your attacks in fire, ice, nature, and lightning. They're gone with the rest of the elemental kit. Four new stances take their place: instead of enchanting your weapons, you change how you fight with them.
Three of the stances change what some of your swordplay and marksmanship abilities do.
Hit them with a Barbed Shot on the way in, and every Rending Cut you land keeps that arrow wound open.
The mirror of Warden. Cut them on the way past, step back with your bow, and keep the blade wound bleeding from range.
In both stances, the refresh only extends a wound you've already opened. It doesn't deepen the wound, and it does nothing if your other bleed isn't on the target.
Work both your ranged and melee attacks and you can keep both bleeds running far longer than either would last alone.
For the fight that has one enemy too many.

This is the off-tank stance. With Survivor up, plus Taunt and Kick, you can hold an enemy in a pinch. Aggro control is still limited compared to a dedicated tank, so it's a way to hold the line for a while, not a replacement for the classes built to do it.

entries.name: Warden Stance - Melee DPS
entries.desc: Your melee attacks hit harder. Hamstring Slice also opens a gap in the target's armor for a few seconds, lowering its armor class. If your Barbed Shot is bleeding on the target, Rending Cut refreshes that bleed to its full duration.

entries.name: Marksman Stance - Ranged DPS
entries.desc: Your bow attacks hit harder.

entries.name: Maiming Shot also snares the target for a few seconds.
If your Rending Cut is bleeding on the target, Barbed Shot refreshes that bleed to its full duration.
Survivor Stance - Off-Tanking
entries.desc: Increases your parry and armor class. Hamstring Slice also slows the target's attacks.

entries.name: Longstrider Stance
entries.desc: Shift to this stance and your group runs faster outdoors, as long as they stay near you. A member who takes damage slows back down for a while, so it's for covering ground, not for fighting.

sections.title: Wound Care
paras: You carry herbs, bandages, and poultices, and have the know-how to use them. It's based in woodsman's craft, but your healing spells require mana to apply.
Formerly the Weak Heal through Greater Heal line. The poultices now run from Weak Healing Poultice up to Superior Healing Poultice.
Formerly the Prickly, Bristly, Brambly, Spiky, and Thorny Tunic line.

entries.name: Healing Poultice
entries.desc: Press a poultice to an ally's wound. It heals them straight away and keeps mending them for a short while after. You have to be at their side to apply it. Each poultice has a chance to draw out a poison and a disease, and the better poultices do it more reliably. For the times a poultice doesn't take, carry cureberries (see Foraging below).

entries.name: Regeneration and Pack Regeneration
entries.desc: Slowly restore health over time to one ally or to the whole group. Both lines arrive earlier now and each gains a new top rank: Exceptional Regeneration and Exceptional Pack Regeneration.

entries.name: Mantle of the Hunter
entries.desc: Your personal protection: more armor class, a thorny damage shield that hurts whatever hits you, and now more Wisdom. It also lets you sense magical effects on what you consider. The whole line starts much earlier than it used to.

entries.name: Barriers
entries.desc: Put a thorny damage shield on someone else. The Prickly through Thorny Barrier line arrives earlier now, and Jagged Barrier is a new top rank.

sections.title: The Campfire
paras: Between pulls the group gathers around the fire, gets its health and mana back, refreshes buffs, and enjoys a bit of downtime together.

Recuperate has a long cooldown, so you won't call a rest after every fight. When you do, it cuts the wait before the next pull. The cooldown also lines up well with buff durations, so the rest break is a natural time to re-apply them.
A group can only benefit from Recuperate every so often, regardless of how many Rangers are in the party. Once you've rested, you'll need to wait a while before another rest does you any good.
With a Hearth, you never have to go looking for a fire to rest at.

entries.name: Recuperate
entries.desc: When the fight's done, gather your group around the fire. Everyone recovers health and mana quickly for a short while. You need the warmth of a campfire to call a rest - any campfire will do, including your own Hearth. You can't fight while you recuperate. Your blows land weakly and you're easier to hurt, so this is for after the pull, never during it. If you're attacked unexpectedly while recuperating, you can click off the buff.

entries.name: Hearth of the Ranger
entries.desc: Build your own campfire. It burns longer than a normal one, and each log you feed it keeps it going longer too.

sections.title: The Wilds
paras: Open country is where you're most at home. This is the part of your kit for finding your quarry, feeding yourself, covering ground, and getting past what you'd rather not fight.
Your pack is never empty for long.
Speed of the Hunter was formerly Speed of the Predator.

entries.name: Tracking
entries.desc: Unchanged. Tracking is still a skill you train at your guild, and it grows as you level. The more skilled you are, the further away you can pick out a creature and follow it.

entries.name: Foraging
entries.desc: Gather food and drink from the wild. What you find is trail food, and eating or drinking it gives you a light resistance to disease or poison. You can also forage cureberries, which cure poison and disease. They used to come from a summoning spell; now you find them yourself.

entries.name: Speed of the Wild, Speed of the Pack, Speed of the Hunter
entries.desc: Outdoor run speed for one ally or the whole group, and a short outdoor sprint for yourself.

entries.name: Shroud, Camouflage, and Invisibility versus Beasts
entries.desc: Outdoor concealment for yourself (Shroud) or a party member (Camouflage), and invisibility to beasts for a party member. Sneak - Move unseen by anything you're behind.

entries.name: Lull Beasts and Nature's Calm
entries.desc: Lull Beasts calms a beast so you can walk closer without drawing it in. It's now a four-rank line, Lull Minor Beasts through Lull Greater Beasts, and each rank can calm tougher beasts than the last. Nature's Calm calms a creature outdoors for a short time. It's also four ranks (Nature's Calm, Nature's Lull, Nature's Peace and Nature's Serenity), and it's rebuilt from the old Unity spell. Terrify Beasts sends a beast running. Formerly Fear Beasts.

entries.name: And the rest of the kit…
entries.desc: Twisting Roots holds a target in place. Beast Speech lets you talk with animals. Salvage Arrows recovers spent arrows. Enduring Breath lets you breathe underwater. All unchanged.

sections.title: Group Support
paras: Formerly Truestrike Aura. The armor it grants replaces the old Woodskin line.

entries.name: Hunter's Focus
entries.desc: Sharpen your group's weapon skills and Dexterity, and harden their armor. It's now a group buff you cast instead of an always-on aura.

entries.name: Protection and Resistance
entries.desc: Poison Protection and Poison Resistance, Corruption Protection and Corruption Resistance, and See Invisibility are all still here.

sections.title: Retained Spell Lines
paras: Several of these moved to new unlock levels as part of a full level-schedule pass.
Thanks for taking the time to look this over, and for your participation in our Beta. We look forward to getting your feedback after you try out the Ranger update during Early Access!

entries.name: Leading Shot - Renamed from Whistling Shot
Wound Care and Protection
entries.desc: Healing Poultice line - Rebuilt from Weak Heal, Minor Heal, Lesser Heal, Heal, and Greater Heal

Prickly, Bristly, Brambly, Spiky, and Thorny Barrier

entries.desc: Burning Embers Line and Insect Swarm Line - The fire and insect damage-over-time lines borrowed from the Druid. Your bleeds do this job now.

entries.name: Imbue Arrows and Imbue Weapon (Fire, Ice, Nature and Lightning) - Replaced by the stances.
Woodskin, Stoneskin, Steelskin, and Diamondskin and the Union line - The armor buffs. The group version's armor now lives on Hunter's Focus.
Snare and Ensnare - Replaced by Hamstring Slice, Tanglefoot, and Marksman Stance's Maiming Shot.
Sense Magic - Folded into Mantle of the Hunter for yourself.
Cure Disease - Your poultices can now draw out disease.
Summon Cureberries - You forage cureberries now instead.

overview: Rogue is one of the classes getting fewer fundamental changes to gameplay and abilities in their update. It will continue to play similarly to how it has in the past, but with some notable changes. For example, poisons have been fleshed out and made available across more of the level ranges, there’s been a slight reduction in the number of interrupt and stun abilities, and Ambush has been rolled into Backstab in a way that streamlines the application of two very similar abilities.

We found that needing to Stealth mid-fight to use an ability wasn’t very satisfying gameplay. You either macro it together so you don’t think about it, or it’s just an extra keypress. We’d rather save those keypresses for something more impactful, and have made some adjustments to try to mitigate that.

sections.title: Stealth Changes
paras: In the update patch, we're relaxing the ability for NPCs to see through Stealth based on their level. We want to make it a bit easier to play in areas slightly above your level, and more obvious when you're at risk.

NPCs that con yellow no longer have any chance to see through Stealth (though some NPCs can always see through it, so caution is still advised). You’ll need to be careful around anything that's a red con, but this gives you two more levels of safety before the aggro range gradually returns in their front arc.

Additionally, See Invisibility no longer sees through Stealth for NPCs or players. The ability to negate Stealth is currently limited to the Archer’s Flare ability and the Beastmaster's Bat pets. In PVP, players will be able to see you in their front arc if they outlevel you, and within one meter at any time.
Vial of Smoke has been fixed and now provides the intended 5 second window where you will not reaggro regardless of the level difference, giving you a chance to get out of the NPC’s vision arc.

sections.title: Poison Updates
paras: Poisons now start much earlier. You gain access to the first Snaring Poison at level 4, and continue to get new types and tiers of poisons through the levels.
There are 3 types of poisons you can learn from the Poison Maker NPCs, and each has 4 tiers with increasing effects:

Poison recipes start by extracting toxins from venom glands, venom sacs, and poison ducts—drops from venomous animals of a level appropriate to the poison tier. You’ll combine these in a vial with one of the activating agents:
We’ll also be adding some experimental poisons over time that won’t show up as a recipe on the vendor. Those will be up to you to discover.

entries.name: Snaring Poison - Slows the movement speed of the target.
Weakening Poison - Slows the attack speed of the target.
Dulling Poison - Slows the casting speed of the target.

sections.title: Backstab and Ambush
paras: Backstab is the core ability for the class and Ambush as a secondary backstab detracted from it, so we've removed Ambush and partially merged its functionality into Stab. Likewise, Double Backstab at 50 has been removed. All the abilities across the classes with this sudden double damage mechanic are being updated similarly.
By removing the mechanic, we can instead roll that power into higher overall damage and gain greater control over the ramp up throughout the level range.

If you’ve been in Stealth for at least 3 seconds, the weapon-based portion of your Backstab damage will be doubled. The intent here is to provide a strong initial attack when beginning a fight in Stealth, and discourage rapidly entering Stealth just for the damage bonus.
At level 35, you’ll unlock the Assassin Trait, which grants you the ability to critically hit on Stab and Backstab.
And finally, the weapon damage scaling on Backstab has been nearly doubled.

sections.title: Swift Strikes
paras: This ability is now toggleable (on the Aura Bar) and has been set as a Tertiary Haste effect, allowing it to stack with most other forms of haste.

sections.title: New Abilities
paras: Beyond the tiering of Stab and the updated Poison repertoire, Rogues will get several other new abilities in this patch.

entries.name: Slice - Deeply slice your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus Bleed Damage. This ability shares a cooldown with other Might abilities and stacks up to two times.
Twin Blades - Deftly strike your target with twin blades, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage per equipped weapon. This ability shares a cooldown with other Might abilities.
Rain of Steel - Shower your target with throwing knives, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage three times. This ability can be used while moving, has no minimum range, and is channeled.

Poison Tolerance / Desensitization - Develop a tolerance to poison, increasing your Poison Resistance. (Your time working with poisons has given you a slight immunity to them, which you can activate with this self only resistance buff.)

Deadly Throw - Skillfully throw a weapon at your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage. Additionally, if your target is below 20% Health, this ability's damage is doubled. (This is an improved version of Throw, proving the Rogue's mastery compared to other classes.)
Escape Artist - Become elusive, removing all Root and Snare effects and briefly granting you immunity to them.
Gambit - Execute a daring gambit, resetting the cooldown of your Uppercut, Stab, and Vial of Shadow abilities if hit within a short period.

sections.title: Moved/Removed Abilities
paras: Avoidance, Incapacitate, and Low Blow have been removed.
Nimble Evasion and Fury of the Assassin are now obtained at levels 20 and 40, respectively.

sections.title: Soloability
paras: As a positional damage class, we’re aware that Rogues have a tougher time than most other classes when it comes to soloing. While Monsters and Memories is a group-focused game, we’d like to give you at least some ability to play solo while looking for a group. We hope that the new ranged abilities, as well as the cooldown resets from Gambit, make this a bit more achievable if you choose your targets well.

sections.title: Pick Pocket, Lockpicking, and Disarm Traps
paras: A rogue is more than a combat machine, and these abilities are important to the feel of the archetype.

In the patch after the ability rework, Pick Pocket will be changing to no longer pull from the mob’s actual loot table, and instead from a pick pocket specific table. This should open up some quest opportunities in addition to being a bit more desirable in group settings.

Lockpicking and Disarm Traps require a bit more work in the world and content before they can come online - the abilities themselves do very little without doors to pick and dangerous traps to disarm. You won’t be seeing these in the next patch, but they are still planned and will make their way in when the content to support them exists.

overview: The Shadow Knight embodies the anti-hero fantasy of a dark and brooding knight, bending souls to their will and learning more dark magic from the study of monstrous creatures. Shadow Knights use drains and debilitations of the body and soul to gain an edge over their adversaries, and in combat use their life draining abilities to supplement a combat style more focused on offense than defense.

In this update, we’ve tried to separate the Shadow Knight from the Necromancer class without sacrificing the most important parts of the class mechanics. There’s some subtle theme switching: command over souls and corruption in place of undead reanimation, as well as custom versions of spell lines that make a bit more sense on a class that spends the majority of their time taking hits in combat. The future Profane Study (monster hunting) system will unlock a unique and flavorful way for these dark knights to acquire new types of power.

sections.title: Pets
paras: The three spell lines of pets shared with the Necromancer have been replaced with a singular pet - a lost soul bound to the service of the Shadow Knight. This Soul Servant is now summoned using a Soul Remnant reagent you’ll siphon from enemies, rather than buying bone chips in a market.
The summoning spells themselves are set up in 4 ranks, creating pets that scale with your level (if a bit behind compared to more dedicated pet classes).
You’ll retain the ability to sacrifice the pet to form a Sacrificial Barrier, and additionally be able to sacrifice them for a damage shield via Wreath of Souls.

sections.title: Melee Abilities
paras: Shadow Strike replaces Slam as the basic Shadow Knight melee ability, making room for Siphoning Slash and Reave as the more powerful and longer cooldown abilities.
Shadow Strike - This attack extends the duration of any of your Shadows dot spells on the target by 6 seconds.

Siphoning Slash - A slightly stronger attack that heals you for 50% of the damage inflicted. Hitting an enemy with this within the last 10% of its life will siphon a remnant of it’s soul, allowing you to bind it to your will as a pet. This ability shares a cooldown with Reave.
Reave - This dedicated 2H weapon attack requires a brief wind up but hits hard with no additional frills.
Goading Bash - This shield ability shares a cooldown with Kick. In addition to interrupting a spell being cast, you’ll generate bonus threat on targets you block for a brief time afterward.
Kick - This basic spell interrupt is usable without a shield, but locks casters out of recasting for less time than a shield bash.

sections.title: Offensive Spells
paras: Soulrend - The lifetap abilities shared with Necromancer have been slightly tweaked into the Soulrend line. These lifetaps cast quickly, but have a shorter range than the Life Drain line had.

Palpitation - This new DOT replaces the Poison line shared with Necromancers and is a combination agility debuff and damage spell. The damage on this spell ramps up over 4 ticks, but deals its full damage faster than the Poison line. The lack of front-loaded damage and ramp up compensate for the fast cast time on the line.
Smothering Shadows - A new line of Shadow spells replaces the shared Necromancer version. These cast faster than the previous versions, but have a shorter duration as well.
Theft of Vigor - A combination Strength and Stamina drain that replaces the previous Drain Strength line of spells.

Grip of Shadow - This ability is used to grab an enemy from afar and pull them to you, interrupting them should they be casting at the time. While this is not a new ability, the range on it has increased from 15m to 20m.

sections.title: Grip of Agony
paras: Grip of Agony has had a substantial bump in its base damage, and now has an additional Stamina based scaling component. Additionally, when under an Unholy Pact from your Aura of the Unholy, Grip of Agony will heal you for 50% of the damage done.

sections.title: Auras
paras: Shadow Knights continue to have the two Auras: Vampirism and Unholy. These two had significant overlap in that they both increased the group’s damage with a health regaining component. Additionally, Unholy was a bit off-theme for Shadow Knight, which shouldn’t be buffing regeneration outright to their group.
Aura of Vampirism - This Aura is unchanged, and provides each member of the group a chance to cast a lifedrain attack on a melee hit

Aura of the Unholy - This ability has been completely reworked and is now a more tank-centric aura. This aura provides a modest Holy resistance buff to your group, while increasing your generated Threat and Parry Chance. Additionally, when your health falls below 25% of it's maximum, call upon an Unholy Pact to protect you. This pact will reduce incoming damage, empower your Soulrend with additional healing, and grant Grip of Agony a lifesteal for half the damage dealt.

sections.title: Buffs
paras: Lord of Shadows - This self only buff replaces the Spellshield line, granting you increased Intelligence, Armor Class, Hit Points, and Mana Regeneration. Your physical stat buffs will come via your Theft of Vigor drain spell.
Wreath of Souls - A new ability and way to use your pet. Sacrifice your pet to place a whirling wreath of souls around you, damaging those who attack you.
Holy and Cold Resistance - These abilities are retained but are now self-only buffs. Note that Aura of the Unholy can provide some Holy resistance to your group.

sections.title: Retained Spell Lines
paras: The following spell lines weren’t specifically mentioned as they are preexisting, but continue to be available after this update.

entries.name: Removed Spell Lines
entries.desc: Skeleton, Zombie, and Ghoul pet (this is now Soul Servant)

entries.name: Swirling Shadows (replaced by Smothering Shadows line)

sections.title: Profane Study
paras: A new theme and mechanic being layered onto the Shadow Knight is the hunting of corrupt entities to empower the knight. This is a planned future system that will be entering the game in a later patch and is not implemented as of the Early Access launch.

Shadow Knights will get a new skill, ‘Profane Study.’ It is used to study, understand, and control the unnatural forces granting power to the most heinous creatures of Eth-ur. By tracking down these abominations, slaying them, and studying their corpse with your Profane Study skill, you’ll be able to improve your existing abilities, or even uncover new forms of power.

overview: Shamans draw their power from the spirit realm: ancestors, old forces, and ghosts of the past. They listen to that power rather than command it, and this update shifts their abilities to match the spiritual theme.

We also wanted to focus on their role as enhancers and debilitators. They make everyone around them better at their job and break down opponents to limit their danger, all while keeping their party topped up with health.

entries.name: Pact of Renewal
entries.desc: Form a pact of renewal with your target, restoring Health every few seconds. (This is your main healing tool. It works best when cast ahead of the damage, rather than after it. The line dropped its old “spores" theme, and receives upgrades at more regular intervals.)

entries.name: Rite of Mending
entries.desc: Perform a rite of mending on your group, restoring Health every few seconds. (This is a party-wide version of Pact of Renewal on a long cooldown. Save it for a fight you expect to go badly.)

entries.name: Communion of Regeneration
entries.desc: Regenerate your group, increasing their Health Regeneration. (This party-wide regenerate is obtained through research.)

entries.name: Spirit Mending
entries.desc: Mend your target, restoring Health. (This is your standard heal with a short cast time. It now has an additional rank at higher levels.)

sections.title: Damage
paras: Shamans aren’t known for their DPS, but they can bring real damage to longer fights. They have two DoT lines with different durations, plus a single direct damage line. Using their resistance debuffs (see below), they can make all of these land harder. Furthermore, their DoTs now stack with those from other Shamans, making multiple Shamans more viable in groups.

entries.name: Ghostly Blight
entries.desc: Engulf your target in ghostly blight, dealing Magic Damage plus additional damage every few seconds. (This is your main DoT line, rebuilt from the old poison line.)

entries.name: Malady
entries.desc: Infect your target with a malady, dealing Disease Damage every few seconds. (This line was retained, gaining two new ranks.)

entries.name: Spirit Bane
entries.desc: Rend the spirit of your target, dealing Magic Damage. (This is your only direct damage line, rebuilt from the old frost spells.)

sections.title: Debuffs
paras: Debuffs are as critical to the Shaman's role as healing. There are three lines: one slows an enemy's attacks, one drains its physical stats, and one strips its resistances.

entries.name: Omen of Lethargy
entries.desc: Afflict your target with lethargy, decreasing their Attack Speed. (This is your signature slow, and often the most useful thing you'll do in a hard fight.)

entries.name: Omen of Enfeeblement
entries.desc: Enfeeble your target, decreasing their Strength, Dexterity, and Agility. (This is a great companion spell to Omen of Lethargy, making enemies weaker, less accurate, and less evasive.)

entries.name: Omen of Susceptibility
entries.desc: Make your target more susceptible to harm, decreasing their Disease, Holy, and Magic Resistance. (This line opens a target up to everything that follows -- your own spirit and disease magic included. One further change is that it now weakens Holy Resistance where it used to weaken Poison.)

sections.title: Buffs and Utility
paras: No other class buffs physical power the way a Shaman does. Between the berserker lines, hastes, and resistance wards, Shamans simply make their group hit harder and take hits better.

This spell requires a Ritual Talisman. (This is a group version of the Berserker Spirit line. It’s obtained through spell research rather than a merchant, and each cast consumes a Ritual Talisman reagent.)

entries.name: Tribal Spirit
entries.desc: Make your group go berserk, increasing their Strength, Stamina, Dexterity, and Agility.

entries.name: Ancestral Wisdom
entries.desc: Invoke ancestral wisdom, increasing your Wisdom and Health Regeneration, and granting you the ability to see invisible entities and magical effects when considering targets. (This is a self-buff.)

entries.name: Ancestor's Eye
entries.desc: Bestow your target ancestral sight, granting them the ability to see invisible entities and magical effects when considering targets. (This provides both See Invisibility and Sense Magic in a single buff.)

entries.name: Aspect of the Bear
entries.desc: Shapeshift into a bear, increasing your Wisdom and Health Regeneration, and granting you the ability to see invisible entities and magical effects when considering targets. (This provides the same stats and benefits as Ancestral Wisdom, but with added bonus of looking like a bear. It will be rewarded from a Shaman quest during Early Access.)

entries.name: Consume
entries.desc: Consume an offering of your own flesh, restoring Mana at the cost of Health. (Trading health for mana is a defining trait of the class, and a large part of why you can keep going long after your mana should have run out.. This spell line remains a valuable source of mana regeneration; however, after looking at how powerful the pre-update effects of Consume were, we've added a 45 second cooldown to the spell line. It’s still tremendously mana efficient and provides a large boost in mana regen per minute, but it was honestly over-tuned previously and needed an update.)

entries.name: Curing Ritual
entries.desc: Cure your group, removing one Disease effect from each member.

entries.name: Ritual of Escape
entries.desc: Cross your group over into the spirit realm, clearing all Threat from aggressive targets and preventing new aggression, rendering them unseen by both the living and undead, granting them the ability to see invisible entities, and restoring Health and Mana every few seconds. (This allows your party to slip away from an encounter to recover. It has a longer cooldown, but can save the day when things go wrong.)

entries.name: Healing
entries.desc: Regeneration

entries.name: Buffs
entries.desc: Berserker Spirit

entries.name: Utility
entries.desc: Cure Disease, Poison

entries.name: Speed of the Wild and Speed of the Pack
Stealth
entries.desc: Invisibility (which now grants See Invisible as well) Invisibility versus Undead

entries.name: Crowd Control
entries.desc: Blind

entries.name: Removed Spell Lines
entries.desc: Cure Blindness - We're removing this from every class as we work through them. Blind effects are short and rarely dangerous enough to earn a spell slot. Electric Protection and Poison Protection - These have been replaced with Holy Protection and Magic Protection. Flameburst - Fire spells never really suited Shamans, and they fit even less now that everything else you cast involves spirits and sickness. Invisibility versus Beasts - This seemed redundant with Invisibility available. Spirit Wolf and Summon Companion - As we mentioned in an earlier update, combat pets are leaving the classes that aren't built around them. Spreading pets across so many classes blurred the differences between them, and the Shaman has plenty of identity without one. Spiritual Armor - This seemed fairly useless with the Berserker Spirit line available.

sections.title: Research and Quest Spells
paras: As you may have noticed in some of the spell footnotes, not everything will be available on a spell merchant.
Keep this in mind when testing out the update. As always, thank you for reading and for your participation in our ongoing Beta. We look forward to hearing your feedback after you try it out!

entries.name: Communion of Regeneration and the higher Tribal Spirit tiers come from spell research.
The Aspect of the Bear line arrives as a Shaman quest during Early Access.

overview: Welcome to the first deep dive into our ongoing class updates!

In these posts, we’ll take an in-depth look at the mechanics, skills, and abilities that are changing for one of our classes. As a class finishes its design pass and is being implemented, internally tested, and tuned, we’ll post an additional update similar to this one. This means there’s a high probability that some aspects will change before they reach the beta servers. Nonetheless, these deep dives should hopefully answer some of the more nitty-gritty questions regarding each class.
First up: the Spellblade.

This class has received a thorough rework and a slight re-theming. The core fantasy of a magic-imbued duelist was compelling, but the previous iterations either relied too much on RNG/luck to get procs, or added flat damage to every attack that was heavily biased toward fast weapons.

Historically, there were also few decisions to be made by the player, with limited ways to express skill or shape the outcome of a battle. The Unstable Barrier ability created some interesting play, but anchored a large part of your DPS on stealing hits from the tank. These are the main issues we’ve tried to address in the class update.
Before we get started, make sure you’ve read the original update overview.
Now, let’s take a look at some of the major abilities in the new Spellblade kit!

sections.title: Infusions
paras: Infusions are stance-like buffs that activate procs and can be “conducted” via the Conduit ability to provide more powerful or useful effects. Infusion procs activate frequently to inflict damage, while having a less frequent chance to apply an additional effect.
Conduit offers you some burst/utility at the cost of a cooldown, making infusion management an important strategic decision.

entries.name: Arcane Infusion
entries.desc: Infuse your weapon with arcane energy, granting you a chance to deal Magic Damage on melee attacks and a lesser chance to activate Arcane Frailty. Arcane Frailty: Strip your target's arcane defenses, decreasing their Magic Resistance. While this infusion is active, the Mana cost of Arcane Spear is reduced. Conduct this infusion to detonate arcane energy upon your target, dealing Magic Damage.

entries.name: Electric Infusion
entries.desc: Infuse your weapon with electric energy, granting you a chance to deal Electric Damage on melee attacks and a lesser chance to stun them. While this infusion is active, the Mana cost of Discharge is reduced. Conduct this infusion to arc electric energy through your target, dealing Electric Damage and stunning them before arcing to another target.

entries.name: Telekinetic Infusion
entries.desc: Infuse your weapon with telekinetic energy, granting you a chance to deal Physical Damage on melee attacks and a lesser chance to activate Kinetic Siphon. Kinetic Siphon: Siphon the kinetic energy of your target, decreasing their Movement Speed and Agility while increasing yours by the same amount. While this infusion is active, the Mana cost of Kinetic Ward is reduced. Conduct this infusion to blast your target with telekinetic force, knocking them back and immobilizing them.

entries.name: Conduit
entries.desc: Conduct your current infusion, channeling it into a unique spell of the same type. Activating this ability places your current infusion on a long cooldown, and all other infusions on a short one.

sections.title: Offensive Abilities
paras: This is your standard attack.
This is a ranged ability that’s useful for pulling, but can also serve as a staple attack when Arcane Infusion makes it more economical.
This is a short range damage spell.
This is a high level offensive cooldown.

entries.name: Infused Slash
entries.desc: Slash your target with an infused blade, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage plus additional damage based on your current infusion.

entries.name: Arcane Spear
entries.desc: Hurl a spear of arcane energy at your target, dealing Magic Damage. While Arcane Infusion is active, the Mana cost of this spell is reduced.

entries.name: Discharge
entries.desc: Electrocute your target with a powerful discharge, dealing Electric Damage. While Electric Infusion is active, the Mana cost of this spell is reduced.

entries.name: Maelstrom
entries.desc: Become a maelstrom of magical energy, increasing your Attack Speed and chance to activate infusion effects.

sections.title: Defensive Abilities
paras: This was formerly Unstable Barrier. The offensive bonus has been removed, making it a purely defensive option.
This is a defensive cooldown that also offers some potential burst damage.

entries.name: Kinetic Ward
entries.desc: Construct a kinetic ward, increasing your Armor Class and absorbing damage received. While Telekinetic Infusion is active, the Mana cost of this spell is reduced. This spell scales with your Intelligence.

entries.name: Deflection
entries.desc: Take a deflective stance, greatly increasing your Parry chance. While Deflection is active, each parried attack will trigger your current infusion effect.

entries.name: Implosion
entries.desc: Create a crushing vacuum around your target, decreasing their Block, Dodge, and Parry chance. When this spell expires, the vacuum implodes, dealing Physical Damage to your target and those around it.

entries.name: Static Field
entries.desc: Place a static field at your feet, periodically dealing Electric Damage to targets within the affected area.

sections.title: Mobility
paras: This is a gap closer.
This is a melee-range ability.

entries.name: Phase Strike
entries.desc: Instantly teleport behind your target, dealing Weapon Ratio Damage, activating your current infusion effect, and removing all stun and immobilize effects. This ability can be used while stunned or immobilized.

entries.name: Seclusion
entries.desc: Seclude your target, reducing your Threat against them, immobilizing them, and teleporting yourself a short distance away.

entries.name: Aura of the Arcane
entries.desc: Envelop your group in an arcane aura, increasing their Intelligence and Spell Damage dealt.

sections.title: How Does It Play?
paras: With this new toolkit, Spellblades can make important decisions during combat, or even before it, if a pull doesn’t go to plan.

For example, they could Phase Strike ahead to an incoming enemy and push it back by conducting their Telekinetic Infusion. Or they could use Seclusion to lock the mob down before it gets to the group, while teleporting back to safety. Maybe before heading back to the group, they drop a Static Field on the foe while it’s locked in place.

When fighting alone, Spellblades will likely want to soften up their opponent with a few Arcane Spears before committing to a melee fight. But do they lock them down with one of their kinetic-based roots first, or do they start the fight in melee with Telekinetic Infusion and hope for some Kinetic Siphon procs to do a little kiting? Maybe they hope their Kinetic Ward can mitigate the damage and get right to business.

In steady group play, Spellblades still rely on procs for a significant portion of their damage while making regular use of Infused Slash. But to deal optimal damage, they’ll need to weave in Arcane Spear, Discharge, or conduct Arcane Infusion.
There’s a few more abilities in the initial kit rollout, so hopefully some fun surprises remain for those who choose this path.

overview: Welcome to our second class deep dive! We’re making great progress on the first four classes in our update queue, so keep an eye out for more of these posts in the near future.

Today we’ll be looking at the Wizard. We’ve already completed the work and are testing their new kit internally. We’re trying to iron out any bugs and oddities before bringing it to the beta servers, but even then, it’s inevitable that we’ll learn something new when it gets into the hands of thousands of players. Expect a bit of iteration as time goes on.

Our plan is to complete a solid first pass on all 18 classes, which involves getting the right abilities in place and making sure each class has its intended toolkit. While this phase does involve some tuning, we’ll certainly need to revisit each class afterward to ensure everything works well and they feel relatively balanced.

Once a set of changes reaches beta, expect further tweaks and tuning if anything turns out to be majorly wrong. There should be a quick turnaround if something’s outright broken, but otherwise, we'll move on to the next class in line with the goal of bringing all 18 to beta as quickly as we reasonably can.
Now, onto the Wizard.
There are a couple of items we mentioned in the initial Wizard class update post that have shifted somewhat.

sections.title: Abilities
paras: While Wizards can definitely teleport allies, we didn’t add any new summoned items in this round. Wizards still summon a short-duration light source, but that’s all for now. Once we finish more updates, we’d like to revisit summoned items across the board, particularly when it comes to the Elementalist.

This was an existing Wizard ability that we got a lot of feedback on—most of it negative. A common concern was that it felt too random or difficult to get a killing blow, particularly in group situations. Additionally, since the amount of mana returned was tied to damage done, crits and resists felt especially bad.

As a result, we’ve decided to move away from this mechanic and instead give Wizards a different way to gain bonus mana that feels within their control. Wizards still get some mana regeneration via a self-buff and from Arcane Invocation every few minutes, but now they’ll also be able to consume Mark of Magic stacks for an immediate mana return. We’ll tune this through playtesting, and look forward to your feedback after you get a chance to try it out.

As we worked through this one, we decided we want to include research as a broader crafting feature for multiple classes. Wizards will get research, but not as a class exclusive. Also, after including a total of 16 damage spell lines for the Wizard, we’re not sure there’s a lot of need to customize spells further. We can revisit this one if necessary in the future.
This one we kept, and you can learn more about it in the Incantations section further down the page.
Let’s go over the major spell lines Wizards will have after this update.
Seal of Magic, Reclaim Magic, and Arcane Acceleration

Seal of Magic is a key part of the Wizard’s arsenal, giving an immediate damage buff for you and your group. With the update, we’re also adding new ways to consume Marks of Magic in return for helpful effects.

Seal of Magic and Reclaim Magic form the core mana regeneration loop. Seal of Magic rewards you for stacking a debuff on the enemy; Reclaim Magic converts that investment into mana, offsetting the mana cost of your spells. When used with the Volley line, Wizards can do a bit of damage while simultaneously restoring mana.

This is Reclaim Magic's aggressive counterpart. Instead of converting stacks into mana, you convert them into a group-wide spell haste, granting your group mates a valuable buff without straying from your regular damage cycle. Note that this is replacing the previous single-target spell haste buff.

sections.title: Damage Spells
paras: Wizards are masters of magic, so it's only right that they get a tool for every situation. Many of their spells have a secondary effect in addition to dealing damage; for example, ice spells snare the target briefly, lightning spells interrupt casting, and arcane spells decrease the target’s casting speed. We kept a good mix of magic, fire, cold, and electric spells, since every Wizard needs a Fireball.

When designing the spell lines, we tried to give each a strong identity, with tradeoffs between damage, cast time, and mana efficiency. These are likely to see continued adjustments in the future as we get more class updates done, so we can ensure that Wizards are the major damage dealers they should be.
This is your fastest direct damage spell line. It's useful for pulling, kiting, and filling gaps when your longer casts aren't safe, but isn’t quite as mana efficient.

These are your highest damage spells with a longer cast time. They make good openers when soloing, or big hits when your group needs to burn something down fast. Wizards get their first Iceblast early on; they can't cast a lot of them before running out of mana, but they sure hit hard!
Volleys are the fastest way to stack Marks of Magic on a target. Marks give increased damage to your evocation spells, or you can consume them for mana or a spell haste buff.
These are your workhorse single-target spells that are efficient enough to sustain through long fights.
These are a great choice when you're facing high-resistance enemies.
Novas are your fastest AoE spells, though they do a bit less damage than Burst spells and radiate out from the caster’s position (PBAoE).
These are targeted AoE spells, so you can hit things further away than you can with Nova spells. The cast times are longer to account for the greater range.
These are also targeted AoEs, but deal damage over time rather than one big hit like Bursts. This means they are a better choice if you're worried about pulling aggro.

sections.title: New System: Incantations
paras: Before we wrap things up, there's one more piece of the Wizard kit worth knowing about: the Wizard-exclusive Incantation system. This was the part we referenced earlier:

Every casting class in Monsters & Memories has ten spell slots available. A Wizard using the Incantation system can access 36 different spells using just five of those slots—four glyphs and the catalyst that fires them. This gives you access to all 16 damage spell lines at any time, along with 20 other utility spells.
That's the pitch.

If you like the fantasy of a Wizard who’s genuinely mastered their craft and always has the right spell for the moment, then this system was built for you. It does come with some effort though, as recalling which glyphs you need for the right incantation can take time and experience as a player. A damage spell is always a combination of two glyphs, but that’s still 16 incantations to recall.

We don’t want to over or under sell this feature. We hope many Wizards will enjoy it, but it's not going to please everyone, and that's okay. Please consider Incantations an optional mastery system. If it doesn’t grab you, every Wizard spell is also available as a traditional scroll you can scribe, memorize, and cast from your bar the traditional way. You can still play Wizard at a high level without ever touching a glyph.

The system unlocks gradually. Wizards get their first glyph at level 8 with only a handful of combinations to learn. A second arrives at 16, a third at 24, and the fourth at 32. By the time all 36 incantations are available, most of the recipe logic should already feel familiar; each element follows consistent patterns, so you're building on rules you've already learned rather than memorizing a table from scratch.

If you’re already a high level Wizard, this system may be a little more challenging to learn all at once compared to ramping up gradually throughout the leveling journey. Please keep that in mind when trying it out.
And a little lore side note: the name of each glyph is based on a language we're developing for an ancient civilization… but you’ll learn more about that as the game grows.

entries.name: “In combat, they can combine magical elements on the fly to adapt to the situation.”
For those who do want to learn it, here's how it works:
entries.desc: Glyphs are the building blocks. There are four of them, with one for each element: Glyph: Mun (Arcane), Glyph: Hil (Ice), Glyph: Nas (Lightning), and Glyph: Dur (Fire). They have no mana cost and don't trigger the global cooldown. Incantations are recipes you build by casting glyphs in sequence. The first glyph you cast sets your foundation; i.e., the spell type you're building toward. Any glyphs you cast after are enhancements that shape the final spell. You can add one enhancement up to two times before activating your incantation. Spell Catalyst activates the incantation, triggering whichever spell your combination maps to at the highest rank you're capable of.

paras: That wraps up our Wizard deep dive. If you've made it this far, thanks for reading. We’ll keep an eye out for feedback and initial impressions, and we really look forward to seeing what you think after you’ve tried this out on the beta server in a couple weeks.
